title.zh: 卷一百八十六下 列傳第一百三十六下: 酷吏下
title.raw: 卷一百八十六下 列傳第一百三十六下: 酷吏下 Volume 186 Biographies 136: Cruel Officials 2

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 序前代賁丘園，招隱逸，所以重貞退之節，息貪競之風。

translations.literal: In prefaces to former dynasties, [rulers] honored those in orchards and gardens and recruited recluses, thereby to esteem the integrity of steadfast withdrawal and to still the wind of greed and rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: In their prefaces, dynasties past honored men who lived among fields and groves and sought out recluses—ways to uphold the virtue of resolute withdrawal and to quell the appetite for gain and rivalry.

sentences.zh: 故蒙叟矯《讓王》之篇，玄晏立高人之傳，箕、潁之跡，粲然可觀。

translations.literal: Therefore the Old Master Zhuangzi fashioned the chapter "The Abdication of Kings," Xuan Yan established biographies of lofty men, and the traces at Ji and Ying shine forth brilliantly for viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi fashioned the chapter "The Abdication of Kings"; Huangfu Mi compiled accounts of lofty men; and the footprints along the Ji and Ying remain luminous to behold.

sentences.zh: 而漢二龔之流，乃心王室，不事莽朝，忍渴盜泉，本非絕俗，甚可嘉也。

translations.literal: Yet the sort of the Two Gongs of Han were loyal at heart to the royal house, would not serve Wang Mang's court, and endured thirst rather than drink from the Stolen Spring—they were in origin not men who cut themselves off from the world, yet most worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men like the two Gongs of Han kept their loyalty to the Liu house, refused to serve Wang Mang, and would go thirsty rather than drink from the Stolen Spring. They were not true world-renouncers, yet how commendable they were.

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐、陶淵明慢世逃名，放情肆誌，逍遙泉石，無意於出處之間，又其善也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi and Tao Yuanming disdained the age and fled from fame, gave free rein to feeling and indulged their will, roamed among springs and rocks, and cared nothing for whether to serve or withdraw—this too was their excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi and Tao Yuanming scorned worldly ambition, lived as their hearts pleased among streams and stone, and gave no thought to office or retirement—and in that lay their virtue.

sentences.zh: 即有身在江湖之上，心遊魏闕之下，托薛蘿以射利，假巖壑以釣名，退無肥遁之貞，進乏濟時之具，《山移》見誚，海鳥興譏，無足多也。

translations.literal: There are also those whose bodies are upon rivers and lakes while their hearts roam beneath the palace gates, who use creepers on cliffs to shoot for profit and borrow mountain ravines to fish for fame—on withdrawal they lack the integrity of a full retreat, on advancement they lack the means to aid the age. "The Moving Mountain" draws mockery, and the sea bird invites ridicule; such men are not worth much praise.
translations.idiomatic: Some keep to the wilds in body while their hearts court the capital, using a hermit's garb to chase profit and a mountain retreat to angle for renown. In retirement they lack true withdrawal; in office they lack what is needed to serve the times. They earn the scorn of "The Moving Mountain" and the ridicule of the sea bird—hardly men to admire.

sentences.zh: 阮嗣宗傲世佯狂，王無功嗜酒放蕩，才不足而智有余，傷其時而晦其用，深識之士也。

translations.literal: Ruan Jizong was arrogant toward the world and feigned madness; Wang Wugong loved wine and lived licentiously. Their talent was insufficient yet their wisdom had surplus; they grieved their times and concealed their usefulness—men of profound understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji defied the age in feigned madness; Wang Jiqin drowned himself in wine and abandon. Short on talent but rich in insight, they mourned their times and hid their gifts—men who saw deeply.

sentences.zh: 高宗天後，訪道山林，飛書巖穴，屢造幽人之宅，堅回隱士之車。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong and Empress Tianhou sought the Way in mountain forests, sent flying letters to cliff caves, repeatedly visited the dwellings of secluded men, and firmly turned back the carts of recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong and Empress Wu sought sages in the hills, sent urgent summons to mountain caves, called again and again at hermits' doors, and just as firmly had their carriages sent back.

sentences.zh: 而遊巖、德義之徒，所高者獨行；

translations.literal: Yet men such as Youyan and Deyi—what they esteemed was solitary conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Yet for men like Tian Youyan and Shi Deyi, what they prized was solitary integrity;

sentences.zh: 盧鴻一、承禎之比，所重者逃名。

translations.literal: men like Lu Hongyi and Chengzhen—what they valued was fleeing from fame.
translations.idiomatic: while for men like Lu Hongyi and Sima Chengzhen, what mattered was escaping renown.

sentences.zh: 至於出處語默之大方，未足與議也。

translations.literal: As for the great norms of serving or withdrawing, speaking or keeping silent, they were not fit to be discussed with.
translations.idiomatic: On the larger question of when to serve, when to withdraw, when to speak, and when to hold silence, they scarcely merit debate.

sentences.zh: 今存其舊說，以備雜篇。

translations.literal: Now their former accounts are preserved to supply the miscellaneous biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Their earlier accounts are preserved here for the miscellaneous biographies.

sentences.zh: 王績王績，字無功，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Wang Ji—Wang Ji, styled Wugong, was a native of Longmen in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, courtesy name Wugong, was from Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少與李播、呂才為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: In youth he formed with Li Bo and Lü Cai a friendship of utter trust.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was the closest of friends with Li Bo and Lü Cai.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，應孝悌廉潔舉，授揚州六合縣丞。

translations.literal: During the Daye era of Sui, he responded to the recommendation for filial piety, fraternal duty, integrity, and purity, and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Liuhe County in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye period he was recommended for filial piety and integrity and appointed assistant magistrate of Liuhe County in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 非其所好，棄官還鄉里。

translations.literal: It was not to his liking, so he abandoned his office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: The post did not suit him, and he resigned to return home.

sentences.zh: 績河渚中先有田數頃，鄰渚有隱士仲長子先，服食養性，績重其真素，願與相近，乃結廬河渚，以琴酒自樂。

translations.literal: Ji already had several qing of fields on the river islet; on a neighboring islet lived the recluse Zhongchang Zixian, who took medicines to nourish his nature. Ji esteemed his genuineness and simplicity and wished to live near him, so he built a hut on the river islet and took his pleasure in zither and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Ji already owned a few acres on a river islet. Nearby lived the recluse Zhongchang Zixian, who nourished his nature through diet and elixirs. Ji admired his plain authenticity, wished to live near him, built a hut on the islet, and amused himself with zither and wine.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊北山，因為《北山賦》以見誌，詞多不載。

translations.literal: Once he traveled to North Mountain and thereupon composed the "Rhapsody on North Mountain" to express his intent; most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited North Mountain and wrote the "Rhapsody on North Mountain" to declare his aims; most of its wording is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 績嘗躬耕於東臯，故時人號東臯子。

translations.literal: Ji once personally plowed at Eastern Mound, so people of the time called him Master of Eastern Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He once farmed with his own hands at Eastern Mound, whence contemporaries called him Master Eastern Mound.

sentences.zh: 或經過酒肆，動經數日，往往題壁作詩，多為好事者諷詠。

translations.literal: Sometimes passing a wine shop, he would stay for days on end; often he inscribed poems on walls, and many were chanted by enthusiasts.
translations.idiomatic: When he lingered at taverns he might stay for days, often writing poems on the walls that enthusiasts loved to recite.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of Zhenguan (644).

sentences.zh: 臨終自克死日，遺命薄葬，兼預自為墓誌。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he himself fixed the day of his death, left instructions for a simple burial, and also beforehand composed his own tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he set the date himself, ordered a plain burial, and had already written his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 有文集五卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected writings in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to five juan.

sentences.zh: 又撰《隋書》，未就而卒。

translations.literal: He also compiled the History of Sui, but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: He also began a History of Sui but died before finishing it.

sentences.zh: 兄通，字仲淹，隋大業中名儒，號文中子，自有傳。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tong, styled Zhongyan, was a famous Confucian of the Sui Daye period, called the Master of Literary Central, and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wang Tong, courtesy name Zhongyan, was a renowned scholar of the Sui Daye era, known as the Master of Literary Central, and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 田遊巖田遊巖，京兆三原人也。

translations.literal: Tian Youyan—Tian Youyan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Youyan was from Sanyuan in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 初，補太學生，後罷歸，遊於太白山。

translations.literal: At first he was selected as an Imperial University student; later he left and returned home, roaming on Mount Taibai.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the Imperial University, then left to wander on Mount Taibai.

sentences.zh: 每遇林泉會意，輒留連不能去。

translations.literal: Whenever he met woods and springs that pleased his mind, he would linger and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever woods and streams caught his fancy, he lingered and could not tear himself away.

sentences.zh: 其母及妻子並有方外之誌，與遊巖同遊山水二十余年。

translations.literal: His mother, wife, and children all shared aspirations beyond the world, and together with Youyan roamed mountains and rivers for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, wife, and children all shared his wish to live beyond worldly affairs, and for more than twenty years roamed the hills and waters with him.

sentences.zh: 後入箕山，就許由廟東築室而居，自稱「許由東鄰」。

translations.literal: Later he entered Mount Ji, built a dwelling east of the shrine to Xu You, and called himself "Xu You's eastern neighbor."
translations.idiomatic: Later he settled on Mount Ji, built a house east of Xu You's shrine, and styled himself "Xu You's eastern neighbor."

sentences.zh: 調露中，高宗幸嵩山，遣中書侍郎薛元超就問其母。

translations.literal: In the Tiaolu era, Emperor Gaozong visited Mount Song and sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao to inquire of his mother.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiaolu period, Emperor Gaozong visited Mount Song and sent Vice Director Xue Yuanchao to call on Youyan's mother.

sentences.zh: 遊巖山衣田冠出拜，帝令左右扶止之。

translations.literal: Youyan came forth in mountain garb and a farmer's cap to bow; the Emperor ordered those at his side to support him and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Youyan came out in rustic dress and a farmer's cap to bow; the emperor had attendants hold him back from prostrating himself.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「先生養道山中，比得佳否？」

translations.literal: He said to him: "Sir, you have cultivated the Way in the mountains—have you lately fared well?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Sir, you have cultivated the Way in these mountains—have you been well of late?"

sentences.zh: 遊巖曰：「臣泉石膏肓，煙霞痼疾，既逢聖代，幸得逍遙。」

translations.literal: Youyan said: "Your subject is incurably addicted to springs and rocks, chronically afflicted with mist and sunset glow; having met this sage age, I am fortunate to roam freely."
translations.idiomatic: Youyan replied, "I am hopelessly devoted to springs and stone, chronically ill with love of mist and crimson clouds; in this enlightened age I am blessed to wander free."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕今得卿，何異漢獲四皓乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Now that I have obtained you, how is this different from Han gaining the Four White-haired Elders?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In gaining you today, am I not like the Han who won the Four White-haired Elders?"

sentences.zh: 薛元超曰：「漢高祖欲廢嫡立庶，黃、綺方來，豈如陛下崇重隱淪，親問巖穴！」

translations.literal: Xue Yuanchao said: "Emperor Gaozu of Han wished to depose the heir and establish a younger son; only then did Huang and Qi come forth—how can that compare with Your Majesty honoring reclusion and personally inquiring at cliff caves!"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuanchao said, "The Han founder sought them only when he meant to displace the heir—how unlike Your Majesty, who honors recluses and visits their mountain caves in person!"

sentences.zh: 帝甚歡，因將遊巖就行宮，並家口給傳乘赴都，授崇文館學士，令與太子少傅劉仁軌談論。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and thereupon took Youyan to the traveling palace; his entire household was given relay carriages to proceed to the capital. He was appointed Academician of the Chongwen Hall and ordered to discourse with the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor Liu Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, brought Youyan to the traveling palace, sent his whole family to the capital by relay carriage, appointed him academician of the Chongwen Hall, and had him converse with the crown prince's junior tutor Liu Rengui.

sentences.zh: 帝後將營奉天宮於嵩山，遊巖舊宅，先居宮側。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor was to build the Fengtian Palace on Mount Song; Youyan's former dwelling happened to lie beside where the palace would stand.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later planned the Fengtian Palace on Mount Song, Youyan's former home stood where the palace was to rise.

sentences.zh: 特令不毀，仍親書題額懸其門，曰「隱士田遊巖宅」。

translations.literal: He specially ordered that it not be destroyed, and personally wrote and hung an inscribed plaque on its gate, reading "Dwelling of the Recluse Tian Youyan."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it spared, wrote the plaque himself, and hung it on the gate: "Dwelling of the Recluse Tian Youyan."

sentences.zh: 文明中，進授朝散大夫，拜太子洗馬，垂拱初，坐與裴炎交結，特放還山。

translations.literal: In the Wenming era he was advanced to Grand Master of Palace Leisure; he was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent. At the beginning of Chuigong, because he was implicated in association with Pei Yan, he was specially released to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: During Wenming he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure and made groom of the heir apparent. Early in Chuigong he was implicated in ties with Pei Yan and specially allowed to return to the hills.

sentences.zh: 史德義史德義，蘇州昆山人也。

translations.literal: Shi Deyi—Shi Deyi was a native of Kunshan in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Deyi was from Kunshan in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，隱居武丘山，以琴書自適。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng he lived in seclusion on Mount Wuqiu, taking his ease with zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianheng he retired to Mount Wuqiu, contenting himself with zither and books.

sentences.zh: 或騎牛帶瓢，出入郊郭廛市，號為逸人。

translations.literal: Sometimes riding an ox and carrying a gourd, he went in and out of suburbs, market towns, and city streets, and was called a man of ease.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he rode an ox with a gourd at his side, wandering suburbs and markets, and was known as a free spirit.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞其名，征赴洛陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong heard his name and summoned him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong heard of him and summoned him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋稱疾東歸。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded illness and returned east.

sentences.zh: 公卿已下，皆賦詩餞別，德義亦以詩留贈，其文甚美。

translations.literal: From dukes and ministers downward, all composed poems to bid him farewell; Deyi also left a parting poem in return, and its wording was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and ministers down the ranks wrote farewell poems; Deyi replied in verse, and his lines were exquisite.

sentences.zh: 天授初，江南道宣勞使、文昌左丞周興表薦之，則天征赴都，詔曰：「蘇州隱士史德義，誌尚虛玄，業履貞確，謙沖彰於裏騕，孝友表於閨庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou, Zhou Xing, Commissioner to Announce Comfort on the Jiangnan Circuit and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized recommending him. Empress Zetian summoned him to the capital. An edict said: "The recluse Shi Deyi of Suzhou—his aspirations are lofty and abstruse, his conduct steadfast and sure; modesty shines in his neighborhood, filial piety and brotherly duty show in his household.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshou, Zhou Xing, commissioner on the Jiangnan circuit and left vice director of the Secretariat, recommended him. Empress Wu summoned him to court. The edict read: "The Suzhou recluse Shi Deyi holds aspirations lofty and pure and conduct steadfast and true; humility is known in his lane, filial devotion in his home.

sentences.zh: 固辭征辟，長往嚴陵之瀨；

translations.literal: He firmly declined summons and appointment and long dwelt at the shallows of Yanling;
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused office and long made his home by the shallows of Yanling;

sentences.zh: 多謝簪裾，高蹈愚公之谷。

translations.literal: repeatedly declined official caps and robes and loftily trod the valley of the Foolish Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: again and again declined court dress and walked the high path of the Foolish Old Man's valley.

sentences.zh: 博聞強識，說《禮》敦《詩》，繕性丘園，甘心畎畝。

translations.literal: Broad in hearing and strong in memory, he expounds the Rites and esteems the Odes, nurtures his nature in orchards and gardens, and is content in field and furrow.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and keen of memory, he teaches the Rites and cherishes the Odes, tends his nature among fields and groves, and is content to till the soil.

sentences.zh: 朕承天革命，建極開階，寤寐星雲，物色林壑。

translations.literal: We have received Heaven's mandate in revolution, established the pole and opened the steps, and waking and sleeping seek stars and clouds, searching forests and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: We have received Heaven's mandate, established the throne, and wake and sleep seeking worthy men among stars and clouds, searching forests and ravines.

sentences.zh: 順禎期而捐薛帶，應休運而解荷裳；

translations.literal: In accord with an auspicious season he cast off his creeper belt; responding to a flourishing fortune he loosed his lotus robe;
translations.idiomatic: In an auspicious season he laid aside his hermit's belt; at a time of flourishing fortune he put off his lotus robe;

sentences.zh: 粵自海隅，來遊魏闕，行藏之理斯得，去就之節無違。

translations.literal: from the sea's edge he has come to roam the Wei palace gate; the principle of acting or concealing himself is thereby attained, and the integrity of going or staying is not violated.
translations.idiomatic: From the sea's edge he has come to the capital; the wisdom of when to serve and when to withdraw is fulfilled, and the integrity of his choices is intact.

sentences.zh: 風操可嘉，啟沃攸佇，特宜優獎，委以諫曹。

translations.literal: His wind and conduct are praiseworthy; we greatly await his counsel. He is specially fit for preferential reward and should be entrusted to the remonstrance office.
translations.idiomatic: His character is admirable and his counsel keenly awaited; he should receive special honors and be placed in the remonstrance bureau.

sentences.zh: 可朝散大夫。」

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Palace Leisure."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure."

sentences.zh: 後周興伏誅，德義坐為所薦免官。

translations.literal: Later Zhou Xing was executed; Deyi was dismissed from office because he had been recommended by him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Xing was put to death; Deyi lost his post for having been Zhou's nominee.

sentences.zh: 以朝散大夫放歸丘壑，自此聲譽稍減於隱居之前。

translations.literal: As Grand Master of Palace Leisure he was released to return to hills and ravines; from this his reputation was somewhat diminished compared with before his reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Released to the hills with the title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, his renown thereafter fell somewhat short of what it had been in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 王友貞王友貞，懷州河內人也。

translations.literal: Wang Youzhen—Wang Youzhen was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhen was from Henei in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 父知敬，則天時麟臺少監，以工書知名。

translations.literal: His father Zhijing, during the time of Empress Zetian, was Vice Director of the Lin Terrace and was renowned for skill in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Zhijing served under Empress Wu as vice director of the Lin Terrace and was famed for calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 友貞弱冠時，母病篤，醫言唯啖人肉乃差。

translations.literal: When Youzhen was in his weak-crown years, his mother was gravely ill; the physician said only by eating human flesh could she recover.
translations.idiomatic: In his early manhood his mother fell gravely ill; the physician said only human flesh could cure her.

sentences.zh: 友貞獨念無可求治，乃割股肉以飴親，母病尋差。

translations.literal: Youzhen alone thought there was no other cure to seek, so he cut flesh from his thigh to feed his parent; his mother's illness soon improved.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhen alone saw no other remedy and cut flesh from his thigh to feed her; his mother soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 則天聞之，令就其家驗問，特加旌表。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian heard of it, ordered verification and inquiry at his home, and specially bestowed commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu heard of it, sent officials to verify the act at his home, and specially honored him.

sentences.zh: 友貞素好學，讀《九經》皆百遍，訓誨子弟，如嚴君焉。

translations.literal: Youzhen had long loved learning; he read each of the Nine Classics a hundred times and instructed his sons and younger kin as a strict father would.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhen had always loved learning, read each of the Nine Classics a hundred times, and taught his sons and kin with a father's stern care.

sentences.zh: 口不言人過，尤好釋典；

translations.literal: He never spoke of others' faults by mouth and especially loved Buddhist sutras;
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke ill of others and was especially devoted to Buddhist sutras;

sentences.zh: 屏絕⺶亶味，出言未曾負諾，時論以為真君子也。

translations.literal: he barred meat and strong flavors, and in speech never broke a promise; opinion of the time held him a true gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: he abstained from meat and pungent foods, and never broke his word; contemporaries deemed him a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 長安年，歷任長水令。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he served in succession as Magistrate of Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an period he served as magistrate of Changshui.

sentences.zh: 後罷歸田裏。

translations.literal: Later he left office and returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resigned and returned to his fields.

sentences.zh: 中宗在春宮，召為司議郎，不就。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace, he was summoned as Remonstrance Secretary but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was crown prince, he was summoned as remonstrance secretary but declined.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，又拜太子中舍，仍令所司以禮征赴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was again appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and the relevant offices were again ordered to summon him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong he was again made attendant of the heir apparent, and the authorities were ordered to summon him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 及至，固以疾辭。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he firmly pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict said:

sentences.zh: 敦夷齊之行，可以激貪；

translations.literal: To encourage the conduct of Bo Yi and Shu Qi can stir the greedy;
translations.idiomatic: Upholding the example of Bo Yi and Shu Qi can shame the greedy;

sentences.zh: 尚顏閔之道，用能勸俗。

translations.literal: to esteem the Way of Yan Hui and Min Sun can thereby exhort custom.
translations.idiomatic: honoring the way of Yan Hui and Min Sun can reform the manners of the age.

sentences.zh: 新除太子中舍人王友貞，德義泉藪，人倫茂異，孝始於事親，信表於行己。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent Wang Youzhen is a spring and marsh of virtue and righteousness, outstanding in human relations; filial piety begins in serving his parents, trustworthiness shows in his personal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed attendant of the heir apparent Wang Youzhen is a wellspring of virtue, outstanding among men; filial piety begins in how he serves his parents, trust in how he conducts himself.

sentences.zh: 富有文史，廉於財貨，久歷官政，累聞課績。

translations.literal: Rich in letters and histories, sparing with wealth, long experienced in government, repeatedly noted for meritorious performance.
translations.idiomatic: Learned in letters and history, sparing with wealth, long in office, and repeatedly praised in performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 有古人之風，保君子之德。

translations.literal: He has the wind of the ancients and preserves a gentleman's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He bears the spirit of the ancients and keeps a gentleman's integrity.

sentences.zh: 乃抗誌塵外，棲情物表，深歸解脫之門，誓守薰修之誡。

translations.literal: He has raised his will beyond the dust, lodged his feelings outside things, deeply entered the gate of liberation, and vowed to keep the precepts of incense and cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He holds his will above the world, his heart beyond things, has deeply entered the gate of liberation, and vows to keep the Buddhist precepts.

sentences.zh: 頃加征命，作護儲闈，固在辭榮，累陳情懇。

translations.literal: Recently he was given an added appointment to guard the storehouse of the heir, yet he firmly declines honor and has repeatedly stated his earnest plea.
translations.idiomatic: Recently honored with office to serve the heir, he steadfastly refuses glory and has repeatedly pleaded his case.

sentences.zh: 堅持凈義，不登於車服；

translations.literal: He steadfastly upholds pure righteousness and will not mount carriage or robe;
translations.idiomatic: He holds to pure conduct and will not take carriage or official dress;

sentences.zh: 惟悅禪綱，味靡求於珍饌。

translations.literal: he delights only in the net of Chan and in taste never seeks fine delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: he delights only in the discipline of meditation and never seeks fine fare.

sentences.zh: 朕方崇獎廉退，懲抑澆浮，雖思廊廟之賢，豈違山林之願，宜加優秩，仍遂雅懷。

translations.literal: We are now exalting integrity and withdrawal and restraining shallow flippancy; though we think of worthies for hall and temple, how could we violate the wish of mountains and forests? He should receive added preferential rank and still be allowed his refined intent.
translations.idiomatic: We now honor integrity and withdrawal and restrain shallow ways; though we desire talent for court, we will not deny his wish for the hills. Let him receive added rank while his refined intent is honored.

sentences.zh: 可太子中舍人員外置，給全祿以畢其身，任其在家修道。

translations.literal: He may be appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent as an extra-staff post, given full salary for the rest of his life, and permitted to cultivate the Way at home.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed attendant of the heir apparent as an honorary post, granted full salary for life, and allowed to practice the Way at home.

sentences.zh: 仍令所在州縣存問，四時送祿至其住所。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties where he dwells are also ordered to inquire after him and deliver salary in the four seasons to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Local prefectures and counties are to inquire after him and deliver his salary each season to his home.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，又表請禮征之，以年老，竟辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, he again memorialized requesting ceremonious summons; because of advanced age, Youzhen finally declined on grounds of illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was crown prince, he again petitioned for a ceremonial summons; Youzhen, now elderly, finally pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 年九十余，開元四年卒。

translations.literal: He was more than ninety years old and died in the fourth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was more than ninety and died in the fourth year of Kaiyuan (716).

sentences.zh: 時下制曰：「貴德尊賢，飾終念遠，此聖人所以治天下、厚風俗也。

translations.literal: At the time an imperial rescript said: "To honor virtue and esteem the worthy, to adorn the end and remember the distant—this is how the sage governs all under Heaven and thickens custom.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript then said: "To honor virtue and esteem the worthy, to adorn the dead and remember the distant—this is how a sage rules the realm and deepens custom.

sentences.zh: 王友貞稟氣元精，遊心大樸。

translations.literal: Wang Youzhen received the primordial essence in his endowment and roamed his heart in great simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhen was endowed with the primordial breath and kept his heart in utmost simplicity.

sentences.zh: 孝惟不匱，獨貫於神明；

translations.literal: In filial piety alone he never failed, penetrating alone to the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: In filial piety he never failed, reaching alone to the spirits;

sentences.zh: 道則難名，高謝於人代。

translations.literal: the Way is hard to name, and he loftily declined the human age.
translations.idiomatic: the Way he followed is hard to name, and he loftily withdrew from worldly generations.

sentences.zh: 言念錫類，方期鎮俗，遽爾雕殂，良深湣悼。

translations.literal: Speaking in remembrance of bestowing favor on his kind, we had just expected him to steady custom, yet suddenly he was carved away in death—truly deep is our compassionate grief.
translations.idiomatic: We had hoped through honoring him to steady the manners of the age, yet suddenly he has perished—our grief is profound.

sentences.zh: 生無大位，雖隔外臣之儀，歿有余榮，宜贈上卿之服。

translations.literal: In life he held no great position; though separated from the rites due an outer minister, in death he has surplus glory and should be granted the robes of a senior minister.
translations.idiomatic: In life he held no high office and stood outside the usual rites for ministers, yet in death he merits honor and should receive the vestments of a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 可贈銀青光祿大夫，仍委本縣令長特加吊祭。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and the magistrate and chief of his home county are entrusted specially to add mourning sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and the magistrate of his home county is ordered to perform special mourning rites."

sentences.zh: 盧鴻一盧鴻一，字浩然，本范陽人，徙家洛陽。

translations.literal: Lu Hongyi—Lu Hongyi, styled Haoran, was originally a man of Fanyang and moved his family to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongyi, courtesy name Haoran, was originally from Fanyang but moved his household to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 少有學業，頗善籀篆楷隸，隱於嵩山。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning and was quite skilled in seal, clerical, regular, and official scripts; he lived in seclusion on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned from youth and skilled in seal, clerical, regular, and official scripts, and lived in seclusion on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遣幣禮再征不至。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, ceremonial gifts were twice sent to summon him, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was twice summoned with ceremonial gifts but did not come.

sentences.zh: 五年，下詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict was issued:

sentences.zh: 朕以寡薄，忝膺大位。

translations.literal: We, meager and slight, have been unworthily granted the great position.
translations.idiomatic: We, meager in virtue, have unworthily assumed the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘗恨玄風久替，淳化未升，每用翹想遺賢，冀聞上皇之訓。

translations.literal: We have often grieved that the abstruse wind has long declined and pure transformation has not risen; we constantly yearn for worthies of old and hope to hear the instruction of the Supreme Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: We have long grieved that the lofty Way has faded and pure custom has not flourished, and constantly yearn for sages of old and hope to hear the teaching of the Supreme Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 以卿黃中通理，鉤深詣微，窮太一之道，踐中庸之德，確乎高尚，足侔古人。

translations.literal: Because you, Sir, are centered and penetrating in principle, plumb the deep and reach the subtle, exhaust the Way of the Grand One, and practice the virtue of the Mean, steadfast and lofty, you are fully the equal of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: You are centered and penetrating in principle, probe the deep and reach the subtle, have mastered the Way of the Grand One, and practice the virtue of the Mean—steadfast and lofty, fully the equal of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 故比下征書，佇諧善績，而每輒托辭，拒違不至。

translations.literal: Therefore we have repeatedly issued summons, awaiting your good service, yet each time you plead excuses, refuse and disobey, and do not come.
translations.idiomatic: We have repeatedly sent summons, awaiting your service, yet each time you plead excuses and refuse to come.

sentences.zh: 使朕虛心引領，於今數年，雖得素履幽人之貞，而失考父滋恭之命。

translations.literal: This has made Us wait with empty heart and outstretched neck for several years now; though we gain the plain conduct and recluse's integrity, we lose the command of Kaofu to increase reverence.
translations.idiomatic: For years we have waited with humble expectation; though we honor your plain integrity as a recluse, we miss the lesson of Kaofu—that reverence should grow with age.

sentences.zh: 豈朝廷之故與生殊趣耶？

translations.literal: Is it because the court's reasons differ in purpose from your life?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that the court's aims and your own differ so greatly?

sentences.zh: 將縱欲山林不能反乎？

translations.literal: Or is it that you wish to indulge in mountains and forests and cannot return?
translations.idiomatic: Or have you given yourself wholly to the hills and can no longer turn back?

sentences.zh: 禮有大倫，君臣之義，不可廢也！

translations.literal: Rites have their great bonds; the righteousness of ruler and minister cannot be abolished!
translations.idiomatic: Ritual has its great bonds—the duty between ruler and subject cannot be cast aside!

sentences.zh: 今城闕密邇，不足為難，便敕賫束帛之貺，重宣斯旨，想有以翻然易節，副朕意焉！

translations.literal: Now the capital gates are close at hand and should not be difficult; We order gifts of silks to be bestowed, this intent to be proclaimed again, and trust that you will have cause to turn about and change your resolve, fulfilling Our wish!
translations.idiomatic: The capital is near at hand and should pose no difficulty. We send gifts of silk and proclaim this intent anew, trusting you will change your mind and fulfill our wish!

sentences.zh: 鴻一赴征。

translations.literal: Hongyi responded to the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 六年，至東都，謁見不拜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he reached the Eastern Capital; at audience he did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he reached the eastern capital and at audience did not bow.

sentences.zh: 宰相遣通事舍人問其故，奏曰：「臣聞老君言，禮者，忠信之所薄，不足可依。

translations.literal: The chief ministers sent a Palace Receptionist to ask the reason. He memorialized: "Your subject has heard the Old Master say that rites are what loyalty and trust thin out and are not sufficient to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers sent a palace receptionist to ask why. He replied, "I have heard the Old Master say that ritual is what loyalty and trust are diluted into—not something to rely upon.

sentences.zh: 山臣鴻一敢以忠信奉見。」

translations.literal: The mountain subject Hongyi ventures to present himself with loyalty and trust."
translations.idiomatic: I, Hongyi, a man of the mountains, present myself in loyalty and good faith."

sentences.zh: 上別召升內殿，賜之酒食。

translations.literal: The Emperor separately summoned him to ascend the inner hall and bestowed wine and food on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him separately to the inner hall and gave him wine and food.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「盧鴻一應辟而至，訪之至道，有會淳風，舉逸人，用勸天下。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lu Hongyi responded to summons and came; We inquired of him concerning the ultimate Way, and he accords with pure custom. To raise up a man of retirement is to use him to encourage all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Lu Hongyi answered the summons and came. We questioned him on the ultimate Way; he embodies pure custom. To elevate a recluse is to encourage the realm.

sentences.zh: 特宜授諫議大夫。」

translations.literal: He is specially fit to be appointed Remonstrance Grand Master."
translations.idiomatic: He should be appointed Remonstrance Grand Master."

sentences.zh: 鴻一固辭，又制曰：

translations.literal: Hongyi firmly declined, and another rescript said:
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi firmly declined, and another rescript said:

sentences.zh: 昔在帝堯，全許由之節；

translations.literal: Of old under Emperor Yao, Xu You's integrity was fully honored;
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Emperor Yao, Xu You's integrity was fully honored;

sentences.zh: 糸面惟大禹，聽伯成之高。

translations.literal: Emperor Yu alone heeded Bo Chengzi's lofty principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yu alone heeded Bo Chengzi's lofty principle.

sentences.zh: 則知天子有所不臣，諸侯有所不友，《遁》之時義大矣哉！

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the Son of Heaven has those he does not treat as subjects, and feudal lords have those they do not treat as friends—how great is the timely meaning of "Retreat"!
translations.idiomatic: Thus even the Son of Heaven has men he does not treat as subjects, and lords have men they do not treat as friends—how great is the timely meaning of Retreat!

sentences.zh: 嵩山隱士盧鴻一，抗跡幽遠，凝情篆素；

translations.literal: Lu Hongyi, recluse of Mount Song, holds his traces aloof in remote seclusion and concentrates his feelings in seal script and plain silk;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongyi, recluse of Mount Song, keeps aloof in distant seclusion and devotes his heart to calligraphy;

sentences.zh: 隱居以求其誌，行義以達其道；

translations.literal: he lives in seclusion to seek his intent and practices righteousness to attain his Way;
translations.idiomatic: he lives in seclusion to fulfill his aims and practices righteousness to attain his Way;

sentences.zh: 雲臥林壑，多歷年載。

translations.literal: He has lain among clouds in forests and ravines for many years.
translations.idiomatic: For many years he has dwelt among clouds, forests, and ravines.

sentences.zh: 傳不雲乎：「舉逸人，天下之人歸心焉。」

translations.literal: Does not the Classic say: "Raise up a man of retirement, and the people of all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you"?"
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Classic say, "Raise up a man of retirement, and the people of the realm will turn their hearts to you"?"

sentences.zh: 是乃飛書巖穴，備禮征聘，方佇獻替，式弘政理。

translations.literal: Therefore We sent flying letters to cliff caves, prepared full rites for summons and appointment, and were just awaiting his counsel in governance to expand political order.
translations.idiomatic: We sent urgent letters to his mountain cave, summoned him with full ceremony, and awaited his counsel to improve governance.

sentences.zh: 而矯然不群，確乎難拔，靜已以鎮其操，洗心以激其流，固辭榮寵，將厚風俗，不降其誌，用保厥躬。

translations.literal: Yet he stands aloof from the crowd, steadfast and hard to draw forth; he calms himself to steady his conduct and washes his heart to stir the current. He firmly declines glory and favor, intending to thicken custom, will not lower his will, and thereby preserves his person.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he stands apart, steadfast and hard to draw forth; he steadies his conduct and purifies his heart. He firmly declines honor, seeking to deepen custom, will not lower his resolve, and thereby preserves himself.

sentences.zh: 會稽嚴陵，未可名屈；

translations.literal: Yan Ling of Kuaiji could not be bent by fame;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ling of Kuaiji could not be bent by fame;

sentences.zh: 太原王霸，終以病歸。

translations.literal: Wang Ba of Taiyuan in the end returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ba of Taiyuan in the end returned home pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 宜以諫議大夫放還山。

translations.literal: He should be released to the mountains with the title Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He should be released to the mountains with the title Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 歲給米百碩、絹五十匹，充其藥物，仍令府縣送隱居之所。

translations.literal: Each year give him a hundred dan of grain and fifty bolts of silk to supply his medicines, and order the prefecture and county to deliver them to his place of seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Each year grant him a hundred dan of grain and fifty bolts of silk for his medicines, and order local officials to deliver them to his retreat.

sentences.zh: 若知朝廷得失，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: If he knows the gains and losses of the court, let him report them fully in memorial form.
translations.idiomatic: If he learns of the court's strengths and failings, let him report them in full.

sentences.zh: 將還山，又賜隱居之服，並其草堂一所，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: As he was about to return to the mountains, he was again granted robes for seclusion and one thatched hall, and the favor and ceremony were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: As he returned to the mountains, he was again given recluses' robes and a thatched hall; the favor shown him was very great.

sentences.zh: 王希夷王希夷，徐州滕縣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xiyi—Wang Xiyi was a native of Teng County in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiyi was from Teng County in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 孤貧好道。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he loved the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he devoted himself to the Way.

sentences.zh: 父母終，為人牧羊，收傭以供葬。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he herded sheep for others and took wages to supply their burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he herded sheep for hire to pay for their burial.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，隱於嵩山，師道士黃頤，向四十年，盡能傳其閉氣導養之術。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, he lived in seclusion on Mount Song, studying under the Daoist Huang Yi for nearly forty years, fully mastering his techniques of breath retention and nourishing life.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he retired to Mount Song and studied under the Daoist Huang Yi for nearly forty years, mastering his arts of breath control and nourishing life.

sentences.zh: 頤卒，更居兗州徂來山中，與道士劉玄博為棲遁之友。

translations.literal: When Yi died, he moved to Mount Culai in Yanzhou and made the Daoist Liu Xuanbo a companion in dwelling and withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, he moved to Mount Culai in Yanzhou and befriended the Daoist Liu Xuanbo as a fellow recluse.

sentences.zh: 好《易》及《老子》，嘗餌松柏葉及雜花散。

translations.literal: He loved the Changes and the Laozi, and sometimes took pine and cypress leaves and miscellaneous flower powders as food.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Book of Changes and the Laozi and sometimes ate pine and cypress leaves and powdered flowers.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，年七十余，氣力益壯。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he was more than seventy years old, yet his vital strength grew ever more robust.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong, though more than seventy, he grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 刺史盧齊卿就謁致禮，因訪以字人之術，希夷曰：「孔子稱『己所不欲，勿施於人』，可以終身行之矣。」

translations.literal: Prefect Lu Qiqing came to visit and paid him respect, then inquired of him concerning the art of caring for the people. Xiyi said: "Confucius said, 'What you yourself do not desire, do not impose on others'—this can be practiced for a lifetime."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Lu Qiqing visited and paid his respects, then asked how to govern the people. Xiyi said, "Confucius said, 'Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire'—one may practice that all one's life."

sentences.zh: 及玄宗東巡，敕州縣以禮征，召至駕前，年已九十六。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong toured east, he ordered the prefectures and counties to summon him with ceremony; he was called before the imperial carriage, already ninety-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong toured the east, he ordered local officials to summon Xiyi with full ceremony. Brought before the imperial carriage, he was already ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 上令中書令張說訪以道義，宦官扶入宮中，與語甚悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Chief Minister Zhang Yue to inquire of him concerning the Way and righteousness; eunuchs supported him into the palace, and the Emperor was greatly pleased in conversation with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Chief Minister Zhang Yue question him on the Way and righteousness; eunuchs helped him into the palace, and the emperor greatly enjoyed their talk.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年，下制曰：「徐州處士王希夷，絕學棄智，抱一居貞，久謝囂塵，獨往林壑。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan a rescript said: "Wang Xiyi, gentleman of Xuzhou, has abandoned learning and discarded wisdom, embraces the One and dwells in integrity, long departed from clamor and dust, and goes alone to forests and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan a rescript said, "Wang Xiyi of Xuzhou has renounced worldly learning, holds to the One, long shunned the world's clamor, and walks alone among forests and ravines.

sentences.zh: 朕為封巒展禮，側席旌賢，賁然來思，克應嘉召。

translations.literal: We, performing the feng and shan rites, have sat sidewise to honor the worthy; he has come with splendor in response to Our excellent summons.
translations.idiomatic: As we performed the feng and shan rites, we honored the worthy; he came in splendor and answered our summons.

sentences.zh: 雖紆綺季之跡，已過伏生之年，宜命秩以尊儒，俾全高於尚齒。

translations.literal: Though his tracks wind like those of the Four Hoary Elders, he has already passed the years of Fusheng; he should be given rank to honor the Confucian, enabling full elevation in honoring age.
translations.idiomatic: Though his path winds like the Four Hoary Elders', he has passed the age of Fusheng; let rank honor him as a scholar and exalt his great age.

sentences.zh: 可朝散大夫，守國子博士，聽致仕還山。

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Palace Leisure, acting Erudite of the Imperial University, and permitted to retire and return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and acting erudite of the Imperial University, and permitted to retire to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 州縣春秋致束帛酒肉，仍賜衣一副、絹一百匹。」

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties are to present silks, wine, and meat in spring and autumn; he is also granted one suit of clothes and a hundred bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: Local officials are to bring silks, wine, and meat in spring and autumn, and he is granted a suit of clothes and a hundred bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 尋壽終。

translations.literal: Soon he died at a great age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died at a great age.

sentences.zh: 自則天、中宗已後，有蒲州人衛大經、邢州人李元愷，皆潔誌不仕；

translations.literal: From the time of Empress Zetian and Zhongzong onward, there were Wei Dajing of Puzhou and Li Yuankai of Xingzhou, both of pure will who would not serve;
translations.idiomatic: From the reigns of Empress Wu and Zhongzong onward, Wei Dajing of Puzhou and Li Yuankai of Xingzhou both held pure resolve and refused office;

sentences.zh: 蒲州人王守慎、常州人徐仁紀、潤州人孫處玄，皆退身辭職，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Wang Shoushen of Puzhou, Xu Renji of Changzhou, and Sun Chuxuan of Runzhou all withdrew from office and resigned, and were praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoushen of Puzhou, Xu Renji of Changzhou, and Sun Chuxuan of Runzhou all resigned their posts and were praised by their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 衛大經衛大經者，篤學善《易》，口無二言。

translations.literal: Wei Dajing—Wei Dajing was devoted in learning and skilled in the Changes; he never spoke a second word.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dajing was deeply learned and skilled in the Changes; he never spoke a careless word.

sentences.zh: 則天降詔征之，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian issued an edict summoning him; he pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned him by edict; he pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 與魏州人夏侯乾童有舊，聞乾童母卒，徒步往吊之。

translations.literal: He was old friends with Xiahou Qiantong of Weizhou; hearing that Qiantong's mother had died, he went on foot to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He was old friends with Xiahou Qiantong of Weizhou; when he heard Qiantong's mother had died, he walked there to mourn.

sentences.zh: 鄉人止之曰：「當夏溽暑，豈可步涉千里，致書可也。」

translations.literal: A fellow townsman stopped him, saying: "It is midsummer's sweltering heat—how can you walk a thousand li? Sending a letter would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor tried to stop him: "It is midsummer's heat—how can you walk a thousand li? A letter would do."

sentences.zh: 大經曰：「尺書無能盡意。」

translations.literal: Dajing said: "A letter a foot long cannot fully express one's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Dajing said, "A letter cannot fully express what I mean."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: And he set out.
translations.idiomatic: And he set out.

sentences.zh: 至魏州，會乾童出行，大經造門設席，行吊禮，不訊其家人而還。

translations.literal: When he reached Weizhou, Qiantong happened to be away; Dajing went to the door, set out a mat, performed the mourning rites, and returned without inquiring of the family.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou, Qiantong was away; Dajing went to the door, performed the mourning rites, and left without asking after the family.

sentences.zh: 開元初，畢構為刺史，謂解令孔慎言曰：「衛生德厚，宜有旌異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Bi Gou was prefect and said to Magistrate Kong Shenyan of Jie County: "Master Wei's virtue is deep and should receive special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Prefect Bi Gou said to Magistrate Kong Shenyan, "Master Wei's virtue is profound and deserves special honor.

sentences.zh: 古人式幹木之閭，禮賢故也。」

translations.literal: The ancients would slow their carriage at Ganmu's lane—such is honoring the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients slowed their carriages at worthy men's lanes—that is how one honors the worthy."

sentences.zh: 慎言造門就謁，時大經已年老，辭疾不見。

translations.literal: Shenyan went to his door to pay a visit; Dajing was already old and pleaded illness, refusing to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan called at his door; Dajing, now elderly, pleaded illness and would not receive him.

sentences.zh: 嘗預筮死日，鑿墓自為誌文，果如筮而終。

translations.literal: He once divined in advance the day of his death, dug his tomb, and composed his own epitaph; he died exactly as the divination had foretold.
translations.idiomatic: He once divined the day of his death, dug his tomb, and wrote his own epitaph; he died exactly as foretold.

sentences.zh: 李元愷李元愷者，博學善天文律歷，然性恭慎，口未嘗言人之過。

translations.literal: Li Yuankai—Li Yuankai was broadly learned and skilled in astronomy, calendrics, and pitch pipes, yet by nature respectful and cautious; his mouth never spoke of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuankai was broadly learned and skilled in astronomy and calendrics, yet respectful and cautious; he never spoke of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 鄉人宋璟，年少時師事之。

translations.literal: Song Jing of his home district, in his youth, took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing of his home district had studied under him in youth.

sentences.zh: 及璟作相，使人遺元愷束帛，將薦舉之，皆拒而不答。

translations.literal: When Jing became chief minister, he sent someone to present Yuankai with silks, intending to recommend him for office; Yuankai refused all and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing became chief minister, he sent silks and meant to recommend him for office; Yuankai refused everything and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，元行沖為洺州刺史，邀元愷至州，問以經義，因遺衣服。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era Yuan Xingchong was prefect of Mingzhou; he invited Yuankai to the prefecture, questioned him on the meaning of the classics, and thereupon presented him with clothing.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong, Yuan Xingchong, prefect of Mingzhou, invited Yuankai, questioned him on the classics, and gave him clothing.

sentences.zh: 元愷辭曰：「微軀不宜服新麗，但恐不能勝其美以速咎也。」

translations.literal: Yuankai declined, saying: "This slight person is not fit to wear new finery; I fear only that I cannot bear its beauty and will hasten misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai declined: "This humble body is unfit for fine new clothes; I fear I cannot bear such splendor without bringing misfortune upon myself."

sentences.zh: 行沖乃以泥塗汙而與之，不獲已而受。

translations.literal: Xingchong thereupon smeared them with mud to defile them and gave them to him; unable to refuse further, Yuankai accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong smeared the garments with mud and gave them to him; unable to refuse further, Yuankai accepted.

sentences.zh: 及還，乃以己之所蠶素絲五兩以酬行沖，曰：「義不受無妄之財。」

translations.literal: When he returned home, he took five taels of plain silk he had raised himself to repay Xingchong, saying: "In righteousness one does not accept unmerited wealth."
translations.idiomatic: On returning home he sent Xingchong five taels of plain silk he had raised himself, saying, "By right one must not accept unearned wealth."

sentences.zh: 先是，定州人崔元鑒明《三禮》，鄉人張易之寵幸用事，薦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yuanjian of Dingzhou was accomplished in the Three Rites; his fellow townsman Zhang Yizhi, favored and in power, recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Yuanjian of Dingzhou was accomplished in the Three Rites; Zhang Yizhi, his fellow townsman then in favor, recommended him.

sentences.zh: 起家拜朝散大夫，致仕於家，在鄉請半祿。

translations.literal: He began his career as Grand Master of Palace Leisure, retired at home, and in his district requested half salary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Grand Master of Palace Leisure, retired at home, and requested half salary in his district.

sentences.zh: 元愷誚之曰：「無功受祿，災也。」

translations.literal: Yuankai mocked him, saying: "To receive salary without merit is disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai mocked him: "To receive salary without merit brings disaster."

sentences.zh: 元愷年八十余，壽終。

translations.literal: Yuankai was more than eighty years old and died at a great age.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai was more than eighty and died at a great age.

sentences.zh: 王守慎王守慎者，有美名。

translations.literal: Wang Shoushen—Wang Shoushen had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoushen enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era he served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuigong he served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時羅織事起，守慎舅秋官侍郎張知默推詔獄，奏守慎同知其事，守慎以疾辭，因請為僧。

translations.literal: When the Luo Weaving affair arose, Shoushen's uncle Zhang Zhimuo, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice, conducted imperial prison investigations and memorialized that Shoushen had known of the matter; Shoushen pleaded illness and thereupon requested to become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Luo Weaving affair arose, Shoushen's uncle Zhang Zhimuo, vice minister of justice, conducted imperial prison investigations and implicated Shoushen; Shoushen pleaded illness and asked to become a monk.

sentences.zh: 則天初甚怪之；

translations.literal: Empress Zetian at first was greatly astonished;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was at first greatly surprised;

sentences.zh: 守慎陳情，詞理甚高，則天欣然從之，賜號法成。

translations.literal: Shoushen stated his case, and his reasoning was very lofty; Empress Zetian gladly assented and granted him the monastic name Facheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushen stated his case with eloquent reasoning; Empress Wu gladly assented and granted him the monastic name Facheng.

sentences.zh: 識鑒高雅，為時賢所重。

translations.literal: His discernment was refined and lofty, and the worthy of the age esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment was refined, and men of worth esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 以壽終。

translations.literal: He died at a great age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at a great age.

sentences.zh: 徐仁紀徐仁紀者，聖歷中征拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: Xu Renji—Xu Renji, in the Shenglü era, was summoned and appointed Left Remembrancer.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Renji was summoned during Shenglü and appointed left remembrancer.

sentences.zh: 三上書論得失，不納。

translations.literal: Three times he submitted memorials discussing gains and losses; they were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he memorialized on the state's strengths and failings; none were heeded.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「三諫不聽，可去矣！」

translations.literal: He said to others: "Three remonstrances unheard—one may depart!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Three remonstrances ignored—it is time to go!"

sentences.zh: 遂移病歸鄉里。

translations.literal: And he pleaded transferred illness and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，宣慰使舉仁紀之行可以激俗，又征拜左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, a Comforting Commissioner recommended Renji's conduct as able to stir custom, and he was again summoned as Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong, a comforting commissioner praised Renji's conduct as able to reform custom, and he was again summoned as left supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 三上書，又不省，乃詣執政求出。

translations.literal: Three times he submitted memorials; again they were not noted, so he went to those in power and requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials again without response, then went to those in power and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 俄授靈昌令。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Magistrate of Lingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Lingchang.

sentences.zh: 妻子不之官，廨舍唯衣履及書疏而已，余無所蓄。

translations.literal: His wife and children did not go to his post; in his office quarters there were only clothes, shoes, and letters—nothing else stored.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children did not accompany him to office; his quarters held only clothes, shoes, and books—nothing else.

sentences.zh: 孫處玄孫處玄，長安中征為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Sun Chuxuan—Sun Chuxuan, in the Chang'an era, was summoned as Left Remembrancer.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuxuan was summoned during Chang'an and appointed left remembrancer.

sentences.zh: 頗善屬文，嘗恨天下無書以廣新聞。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled at literary composition and once grieved that all under Heaven had no book to broaden news.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at writing and once lamented that the realm had no book to spread news widely.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，功臣桓彥範等用事，處玄遺彥範書，論時事得失，彥範竟不用其言，乃去官還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, the meritorious minister Huan Yanfan and others held power; Chuxuan sent Yanfan a letter discussing the gains and losses of current affairs. Yanfan in the end did not employ his words, so Chuxuan left office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong, when Huan Yanfan and other meritorious officials held power, Chuxuan sent Yanfan a letter on the state's strengths and failings. Yanfan ignored his advice, and Chuxuan resigned to return home.

sentences.zh: 以病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 白履忠白履忠，陳留浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Bai Lüzhong—Bai Lüzhong was a native of Junyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Lüzhong was from Junyi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 博涉文史。

translations.literal: He ranged broadly through letters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly versed in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 嘗隱居於古大梁城，時人號為梁丘子。

translations.literal: He once lived in seclusion in the old city of Daliang; people of the time called him Master of Liang Hill.
translations.idiomatic: He once lived in seclusion in the old city of Daliang; contemporaries called him Master of Liang Hill.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，征拜校書郎。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was summoned and appointed Collator.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingyun he was summoned and appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 尋棄官而歸。

translations.literal: Soon he abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，刑部尚書王誌愔表薦履忠隱居讀書，貞苦守操，有古人之風，堪代褚無量、馬懷素入閣侍讀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, Wang Zhian, Minister of Justice, memorialized recommending Lüzhong for living in seclusion and reading books, steadfast and bitter in keeping his conduct, having the wind of the ancients, fit to replace Chu Wuliang and Ma Huai-su as readers-in-waiting in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, Minister of Justice Wang Zhian recommended Lüzhong, who lived in seclusion studying books, steadfast in hardship, with the spirit of the ancients, as fit to replace Chu Wuliang and Ma Huaisu as readers in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 十七年，國子祭酒楊瑒箓又表薦履忠堪為學官，乃征赴京師。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Yang Chang, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, again memorialized recommending Lüzhong as fit to be an academic official, and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Chancellor of Education Yang Chang again recommended Lüzhong as fit for an academic post, and he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及至，履忠辭以老病，不任職事。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Lüzhong declined on grounds of old age and illness, saying he could not bear official duties.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Lüzhong pleaded old age and illness and said he could not serve.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「處士前秘書省校書郎白履忠，學優緗簡，道賁丘園，探賾以見其微，隱居能達其誌。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The gentleman, former Collator of the Secretariat Bai Lüzhong, excels in learning among silk and bamboo, honors the Way in orchards and gardens, probes the profound to reveal its subtlety, and in seclusion can fulfill his intent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The gentleman Bai Lüzhong, former collator of the Secretariat, excels in learning, honors the Way among fields and groves, probes the profound to reveal its subtlety, and in seclusion fulfills his aims.

sentences.zh: 故以汲引洙、泗，物色夷門，素風自高，玄冕非貴。

translations.literal: Therefore We draw him from Zhu and Si, seek him at the Yi Gate; his plain wind is naturally lofty, and the dark cap is not precious to him.
translations.idiomatic: We draw him from the schools of Zhu and Si and seek him at the Yi Gate; his plain integrity is naturally lofty, and the court cap is not precious to him.

sentences.zh: 几杖雲暮，章秩宜加，俾承禮命之優，式副寵賢之美。

translations.literal: With staff and armrest in twilight clouds, rank and order should be increased, enabling him to receive the favor of ritual appointment and fulfilling the beauty of honoring the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twilight of his years, rank should be added, that he may receive the honor of ritual appointment and fulfill our wish to honor the worthy.

sentences.zh: 可朝散大夫。」

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Palace Leisure."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure."

sentences.zh: 履忠尋表請還鄉，手詔曰：「孝悌立身，靜退放俗，年過從耄，不雜風塵。

translations.literal: Lüzhong soon memorialized requesting return to his home district. An imperial letter said: "Filial piety and fraternal duty establish the person; quiet withdrawal releases one from custom; passing the years one follows old age and does not mingle with wind and dust.
translations.idiomatic: Lüzhong soon asked to return home. An imperial letter said, "Filial piety and brotherly duty establish the person; quiet withdrawal frees one from worldly ways; in advanced age one keeps clear of the world's dust.

sentences.zh: 盛德予聞，通班是錫，豈惟旌賁山藪，實欲獎勸人倫。

translations.literal: Your abundant virtue I have heard; regular court rank is granted you — is it only to honor recluses in mountain wilds? In truth it seeks to encourage and exhort human relations.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard of your great virtue, and regular court rank is granted to you — not merely to honor a recluse in the hills, but truly to encourage proper human conduct.

sentences.zh: 且遊上京，徐還故裏。」

translations.literal: Moreover, visit the upper capital, and slowly return to your old home district."
translations.idiomatic: Visit the capital first, then return home at your leisure."

sentences.zh: 乃停留數月而歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon remained several months and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed several months and then returned home.

sentences.zh: 履忠鄉人左庶子吳兢謂履忠曰：「吾子家室屢空，竟不沾鬥米匹帛，雖得五品，何益於實也？」

translations.literal: Lüzhong's fellow townsman, Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Wu Jing, said to Lüzhong: "Your household is often empty; you never received even a peck of grain or a bolt of cloth — though you gained fifth rank, what practical benefit is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Lüzhong's fellow townsman Wu Jing, Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, said to him, "Your household is often destitute; you never received so much as a peck of grain or a bolt of cloth — even with fifth rank, what real good does it do?"

sentences.zh: 履忠欣然曰：「往歲契丹入寇，家家盡著括排門夫，履忠特以少讀書籍，縣司放免，至今惶愧。

translations.literal: Lüzhong said gladly: "In years past when the Khitan invaded, every household was registered for conscripted labor at the door; Lüzhong alone was exempted by the county office for having read a little, and to this day I feel shame and remorse.
translations.idiomatic: Lüzhong replied cheerfully, "When the Khitan raided years ago, every household was registered for corvée at the door. I alone was exempted by the county office because I had read a little — and I still feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 今雖不得，且是吾家終身高臥，免徭役，豈易得也！」

translations.literal: Though I may not receive it now, still our family can lie at home for life, exempt from corvée — how easily obtained is that!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I receive nothing now, our whole family can stay home for life, free of corvée — how rare a blessing is that!"

sentences.zh: 尋壽終。

translations.literal: Soon he died at a ripe old age.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 著《三玄精辯論》一卷，註《老子》及《黃庭內景經》，有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote one fascicle of Refined Discussions of the Three Mysteries, annotated the Laozi and the Yellow Court Inner Landscape Scripture, and had collected writings in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote one fascicle of Refined Discussions of the Three Mysteries, annotated the Laozi and the Yellow Court Inner Landscape Scripture, and left a collected writings in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 王遠知道士王遠知，瑯邪人也。

translations.literal: The Daoist priest Wang Yuanzhi — Wang Yuanzhi was a native of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist priest Wang Yuanzhi was a native of Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖景賢，梁江州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingxian was Governor of Jiang Province under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingxian had been governor of Jiang Province under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父曇選，陳揚州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Tanxuan was Governor of Yang Province under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanxuan had been governor of Yang Province under Chen.

sentences.zh: 遠知母，梁駕部郎中丁超女也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi's mother was the daughter of Ding Chao, Director in the Department of Transport under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi's mother was the daughter of Ding Chao, a director in the Department of Transport under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 嘗晝寢，夢靈鳳集其身，因而有娠，又聞腹中啼聲，沙門寶誌謂曇選曰：「生子當為神仙之宗伯也。」

translations.literal: Once during a daytime nap she dreamed a spirit phoenix alighted upon her body, and thus became pregnant; moreover she heard crying sounds from within her womb. The monk Baozhi said to Tanxuan: "The child born will become chief patriarch among immortals."
translations.idiomatic: Once while napping during the day she dreamed that a spirit phoenix settled upon her, and she became pregnant; she also heard crying from within her womb. The monk Baozhi told Tanxuan, "The child you bear will become chief patriarch among the immortals."

sentences.zh: 遠知少聰敏，博綜群書。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi from youth was clever and quick, broadly mastering all books.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuanzhi was clever and quick-witted, and he mastered a wide range of books.

sentences.zh: 初入茅山，師事陶弘景，傳其道法。

translations.literal: When he first entered Maoshan, he studied under Tao Hongjing and received transmission of his Daoist methods.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered Mount Mao, he studied under Tao Hongjing and received the transmission of his Daoist methods.

sentences.zh: 後又師事宗道先生臧兢。

translations.literal: Later he also studied under Master Zongdao, Zang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also studied under Master Zongdao, Zang Jing.

sentences.zh: 陳主聞其名，召入重陽殿，令講論，甚見嗟賞。

translations.literal: The Chen sovereign heard his reputation, summoned him to the Chongyang Hall to lecture and discuss, and greatly admired and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler heard of his reputation, summoned him to the Chongyang Hall to lecture, and greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 及隋煬帝為晉王，鎮揚州，使王子相、柳顧言相次召之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui was Prince of Jin, stationed at Yangzhou, he sent Wang Zixiang and Liu Guyin in succession to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Yang of Sui was Prince of Jin at Yangzhou, he sent Wang Zixiang and Liu Guyin in turn to summon him.

sentences.zh: 遠知乃來謁見，斯須而鬚髮變白，晉王懼而遣之，少頃又復其舊。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi then came to call upon him; in an instant his beard and hair turned white. The Prince of Jin was frightened and sent him away; shortly afterward they reverted to what they had been.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi came to pay his respects, and in an instant his beard and hair turned white. The Prince of Jin was alarmed and sent him away; shortly afterward they returned to normal.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸涿郡，遣員外郎崔鳳舉就邀之，遠知見於臨朔宮，煬帝親執弟子之禮，敕都城起玉清玄壇以處之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Zhuo commandery, he dispatched Vice Director Cui Fengju to go invite him. Yuanzhi was received at Linsuo Palace; the Emperor personally performed the rites of a disciple and ordered that a Jade Clarity Mysterious Altar be erected in the capital to lodge him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang visited Zhuo commandery, he sent Vice Director Cui Fengju to invite him. Yuanzhi was received at Linsuo Palace; the Emperor personally performed the rites of a disciple and ordered a Jade Clarity Mysterious Altar built in the capital for his residence.

sentences.zh: 及幸揚州，遠知諫不宜遠去京國，煬帝不從。

translations.literal: When he traveled to Yangzhou, Yuanzhi remonstrated that one ought not go far from the capital; Emperor Yang did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor traveled to Yangzhou, Yuanzhi advised that he should not leave the capital so far behind; Emperor Yang did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 高祖之龍潛也，遠知嘗密傳符命。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was still in obscurity, Yuanzhi once secretly transmitted to him the mandate of the talisman.
translations.idiomatic: While the High Ancestor was still in obscurity, Yuanzhi once secretly conveyed to him the talismanic mandate of rule.

sentences.zh: 武德中，太宗平王世充，與房玄齡微服以謁之。

translations.literal: During the Wude era, when Taizong had pacified Wang Shichong, he and Fang Xuanling in plain clothes went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude period, after Taizong had defeated Wang Shichong, he and Fang Xuanling visited Yuanzhi in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 遠知迎謂曰：「此中有聖人，得非秦王乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanzhi met them and said: "Among you is a sage — could it be the Prince of Qin?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi greeted them and said, "There is a sage among you — could it be the Prince of Qin?"

sentences.zh: 太宗因以實告。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon told him the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong thereupon told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 遠知曰：「方作太平天子，願自惜也。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhi said: "You are about to become the Son of Heaven in an age of peace — I hope you will cherish yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi said, "You are about to become Son of Heaven in an age of peace — take care of yourself."

sentences.zh: 太宗登極，將加重位，固請歸山。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, he was about to confer further high rank, but Yuanzhi firmly requested to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, he was about to grant him higher rank, but Yuanzhi firmly asked to return to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 至貞觀九年，敕潤州於茅山置太受觀，並度道士二十七人。

translations.literal: By the ninth year of Zhenguan, an edict ordered Runzhou to establish the Taisou Abbey on Maoshan and altogether ordain twenty-seven Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, an edict ordered Runzhou to establish the Taisou Abbey on Mount Mao and ordain twenty-seven Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 降璽書曰：「先生操履夷簡，德業沖粹，屏棄塵雜，棲誌虛玄，吐故納新，食芝餌術，念眾妙於三清之表，返華發於百齡之外，道邁前烈，聲高自古。

translations.literal: An imperial letter was issued saying: "Master, your conduct is serene and simple, your virtue and achievement pure and refined. You have cast aside worldly distractions and lodged your aspiration in the void and mysterious. Expelling the old and taking in the new, eating spirit fungi and ingesting elixir arts — you contemplate all wonders beyond the Three Pures and restore black hair beyond a hundred years. Your Way surpasses former exemplars; your renown towers from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter said, "Master, your conduct is serene and plain, your virtue pure and refined. You have cast off worldly distractions and fixed your mind on the mysterious void. Expelling the old and drawing in the new, eating spirit fungi and ingesting elixirs — you contemplate all wonders beyond the Three Pures and restore black hair past a hundred years. Your Way surpasses former exemplars; your fame has towered since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 非夫得秘訣於金壇，受幽文於玉笈者，其孰能與此乎！

translations.literal: Were it not one who gained secret formulas from the golden altar and received hidden writings from the jade casket — who could equal this!
translations.idiomatic: Unless one has gained secret formulas from the golden altar and received hidden writings from the jade casket, who could equal this!

sentences.zh: 朕昔在籓朝，早獲問道，眷言風範，無忘寤寐。

translations.literal: I, in former days in the princely court, early gained instruction in the Way; I cherish your manner and model and do not forget you waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: When I was still in the princely court I early received instruction from you; I cherish your manner and never forget you, waking or asleep.

sentences.zh: 近覽來奏，請歸舊山，已有別敕，不違高誌，並許置觀，用表宿心。

translations.literal: Recently reading your memorial requesting return to your old mountain — there is already a separate edict not opposing your lofty resolve, and permission to establish an abbey as well, to express your long-held wish.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your recent memorial asking to return to your old mountain, I have already issued a separate edict honoring your lofty resolve and permitting an abbey to be built, in recognition of your long-held wish.

sentences.zh: 未知先生早晚已屆江外，所營棟宇，何當就功？

translations.literal: I do not know whether you, Master, have already arrived beyond the Yangtze, sooner or later; the halls you are building — when will they be completed?
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether you have already reached the country beyond the Yangtze; when will the halls you are building be finished?

sentences.zh: 佇聞委曲，副茲引領。

translations.literal: I await hearing the details, to satisfy this eager longing.
translations.idiomatic: I await full word of it, to satisfy this eager longing.

sentences.zh: 近已令太史薛頤等往詣，令宣朕意。」

translations.literal: Recently I have ordered Grand Astrologer Xue Yi and others to go visit you and convey my intention."
translations.idiomatic: I have recently ordered Grand Astrologer Xue Yi and others to visit you and convey my wishes."

sentences.zh: 其年，遠知謂弟子籓師正曰：「吾見仙格，以吾小時誤損一童子吻，不得白日升天。

translations.literal: That year, Yuanzhi told his disciple Pan Shizheng: "I have seen the immortal's register: because in my youth I accidentally injured a child's mouth, I cannot ascend to Heaven in broad daylight.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yuanzhi told his disciple Pan Shizheng, "I have seen the immortal register: because in my youth I accidentally injured a child's mouth, I cannot ascend to Heaven in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 見署少室伯，將行在即。」

translations.literal: I see my appointment as Earl of Shaoshi; my departure is imminent."
translations.idiomatic: I see that I am appointed Earl of Shaoshi; my departure is near."

sentences.zh: 翌日，沐浴，加冠衣，焚香而寢。

translations.literal: The next day he bathed, put on cap and robes, burned incense, and lay down to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he bathed, put on cap and robes, burned incense, and lay down.

sentences.zh: 卒，年一百二十六歲。

translations.literal: He died at one hundred twenty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of one hundred twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 調露二年，追贈遠知太中大夫，謚曰升真先生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiaolu, Yuanzhi was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace and given the posthumous title Master Who Ascended to Truth.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiaolu, Yuanzhi was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace and given the posthumous title Master Who Ascended to Truth.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court, he was posthumously granted Supervisory Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held court, he was posthumously made Supervisory Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，改謚曰升玄先生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, his posthumous title was changed to Master Who Ascended to Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou, his posthumous title was changed to Master Who Ascended to Mystery.

sentences.zh: 潘師正潘師正，趙州贊皇人也。

translations.literal: Pan Shizheng — Pan Shizheng was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shizheng was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少喪母，廬於墓側，以至孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his mother in youth and built a hut beside her tomb; he was known for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother in youth and lived in a hut beside her tomb; he was known for supreme filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 大業中，度為道士，師事王遠知，盡以道門隱訣及符箓授之。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he was ordained a Daoist priest, studied under Wang Yuanzhi, who fully transmitted to him the Daoist school's hidden formulas and talisman registers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye period he was ordained a Daoist priest and studied under Wang Yuanzhi, who fully transmitted to him the school's hidden formulas and talisman registers.

sentences.zh: 師正清凈寡欲，居於嵩山之逍遙谷，積二十余年，但服松葉飲水而已。
