translations.literal: Shizheng was pure, quiet, and of few desires. He lived in Xiaoyao Valley on Mount Song for more than twenty years, eating only pine needles and drinking water.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng was pure and of few desires. He lived in Xiaoyao Valley on Mount Song for more than twenty years, eating only pine needles and drinking water.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸東都，因召見與語，問師正：「山中有何所須？」

translations.literal: When Gaozong visited the Eastern Capital, he summoned Shizheng to converse and asked: "What do you need in the mountains?"
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong visited the Eastern Capital, he summoned Shizheng to speak with him and asked, "What do you need in the mountains?"

sentences.zh: 師正對曰：「所須松樹清泉，山中不乏。」

translations.literal: Shizheng replied: "What I need — pine trees and clear springs — the mountains do not lack."
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng replied, "What I need — pine trees and clear springs — the mountains have in plenty."

sentences.zh: 高宗與天後甚尊敬之，留連信宿而還。

translations.literal: Gaozong and the Empress were greatly respectful toward him; they lingered two nights and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong and Empress Wu treated him with great respect and stayed two nights before returning.

sentences.zh: 尋敕所司於師正所居造崇唐觀，嶺上別起精思觀以處之。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered the relevant offices to build the Chongtang Abbey at Shizheng's dwelling, and separately erect the Jingsi Abbey on the ridge to lodge him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered the relevant offices to build the Chongtang Abbey at Shizheng's dwelling and separately erect the Jingsi Abbey on the ridge for his residence.

sentences.zh: 初置奉天宮，帝令所司於逍遙谷口特開一門，號曰仙遊門；

translations.literal: When the Fengtian Palace was first established, the Emperor ordered the offices to open a special gate at the mouth of Xiaoyao Valley, named the Gate of Immortal Roaming;
translations.idiomatic: When the Fengtian Palace was first established, the Emperor ordered a special gate opened at the mouth of Xiaoyao Valley, called the Gate of Immortal Roaming;

sentences.zh: 又於苑北面置尋真門，皆為師正立名焉。

translations.literal: He also placed the Gate of Seeking Truth on the north side of the park — all these names were established for Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also placed the Gate of Seeking Truth on the north side of the park — all these names were created for Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 時太常奏新造樂曲，帝又令以《祈仙》、《望仙》、《翹仙》為名。

translations.literal: At the time the Court of Sacrifices presented newly composed musical pieces; the Emperor also ordered them named Praying to Immortals, Gazing at Immortals, and Raising toward Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Court of Sacrifices presented newly composed musical pieces, and the Emperor also ordered them named Praying to Immortals, Gazing at Immortals, and Raising toward Immortals.

sentences.zh: 前後贈詩，凡數十首。

translations.literal: Poems bestowed on him before and after totaled several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Poems bestowed on him before and after totaled several dozen.

sentences.zh: 師正以永淳元年卒，時年九十八。

translations.literal: Shizheng died in the first year of Yongchun, at ninety-eight years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng died in the first year of Yongchun at the age of ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 高宗及天後追思不已，贈太中大夫，賜謚曰體玄先生。

translations.literal: Gaozong and the Empress recalled him without end, granted him Grand Master of the Palace, and bestowed the posthumous title Master Who Embodied Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong and Empress Wu remembered him with unceasing fondness, granted him Grand Master of the Palace, and bestowed the posthumous title Master Who Embodied Mystery.

sentences.zh: 劉道合道士劉道合者，陳州宛丘人。

translations.literal: Liu Daohe — the Daoist priest Liu Daohe was a native of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist priest Liu Daohe was a native of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初與潘師正同隱於嵩山。

translations.literal: At first he recluded himself on Mount Song together with Pan Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: At first he lived in reclusion on Mount Song together with Pan Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞其名，令於隱所置太一觀以居之。

translations.literal: Gaozong heard his reputation and ordered the Taiyi Abbey established at his hermitage for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong heard of his reputation and ordered the Taiyi Abbey built at his hermitage for his residence.

sentences.zh: 召入宮中，深尊禮之。

translations.literal: He was summoned into the palace and deeply honored.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the palace and treated with deep respect.

sentences.zh: 及將封太山，屬久雨，帝令道合於儀鸞殿作止雨之術，俄而霽朗，帝大悅。

translations.literal: When about to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, prolonged rain intervened; the Emperor ordered Daohe to perform rain-stopping arts in the Hall of Ceremonial Regalia. Soon it cleared; the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was about to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, prolonged rain set in; he ordered Daohe to perform rain-stopping rites in the Hall of Ceremonial Regalia. Soon the sky cleared, and the Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 又令道合馳傳先上太山，以祈福祐。

translations.literal: He also ordered Daohe to travel by post relay to ascend Mount Tai first, to pray for blessings and protection.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Daohe to travel by post relay to ascend Mount Tai ahead of him and pray for divine blessing.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜，皆散施貧乏，未嘗有所蓄積。

translations.literal: Rewards given before and after he distributed to the poor; he never accumulated anything.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards given him before and after he distributed to the poor; he never kept anything for himself.

sentences.zh: 高宗又令道合合還丹，丹成而上之。

translations.literal: Gaozong also ordered Daohe to compound elixir pills; when the elixir was complete he presented it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong also ordered Daohe to compound elixir pills; when the elixir was finished he presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，卒。

translations.literal: During the Xianheng era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xianheng period.

sentences.zh: 及帝營奉天宮，遷道合之殯室，弟子開棺將改葬，其屍惟有空皮，而背上開拆，有似蟬蛻，盡失其齒骨，眾謂屍解。

translations.literal: When the Emperor built the Fengtian Palace and moved Daohe's coffin chamber, disciples opened the coffin intending reburial. The corpse was only an empty skin; the back was split open like a cicada's slough, teeth and bones entirely gone — the multitude said it was corporeal dissolution.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor built the Fengtian Palace and moved Daohe's coffin chamber, disciples opened the coffin to rebury him. The corpse was only an empty skin; the back was split open like a cicada's slough, teeth and bones entirely gone — everyone said it was corporeal dissolution.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞之，不悅，曰：「劉師為我合丹，自服仙去。

translations.literal: Gaozong heard this, was displeased, and said: "Master Liu compounded elixir for me, then took it himself and departed as an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong heard this and was displeased. He said, "Master Liu compounded elixir for me, then took it himself and departed as an immortal.

sentences.zh: 其所進者，亦無異焉！」

translations.literal: What he presented to me was no different!"
translations.idiomatic: What he presented to me was no different!"

sentences.zh: 司馬承禎道士司馬承禎，字子微。

translations.literal: The Daoist priest Sima Chengzhen, courtesy name Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist priest Sima Chengzhen, courtesy name Ziwei.

sentences.zh: 河內溫人，周晉州刺史、瑯邪公裔玄孫。

translations.literal: A native of Wen in Henei; great-great-grandson of Yi Xuan, Governor of Jin Province under Zhou and Marquis of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Wen in Henei and the great-great-grandson of Yi Xuan, governor of Jin Province under the Northern Zhou and Marquis of Langya.

sentences.zh: 少好學，薄於為吏，遂為道士。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and had little taste for serving as an official; he became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and had little taste for office, so he became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 事籓師正，傳其符箓及辟谷導引服餌之術。

translations.literal: He served Pan Shizheng and received transmission of talisman registers and arts of grain avoidance, guided breathing, and medicinal ingestion.
translations.idiomatic: He served Pan Shizheng and received the transmission of talisman registers and the arts of grain avoidance, guided breathing, and medicinal ingestion.

sentences.zh: 師正特賞異之，謂曰：「我自陶隱居傳正一之法，至汝四葉矣。」

translations.literal: Shizheng especially valued and admired him, saying: "From my receiving the Way of Orthodox Oneness from Master Tao the Recluse, to you is the fourth generation."
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng especially admired him and said, "From the time I received the Way of Orthodox Oneness from Master Tao the Recluse, you are the fourth generation."

sentences.zh: 承禎嘗遍遊名山，乃止於天臺山。

translations.literal: Chengzhen once traveled widely among famous mountains, then settled on Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen once traveled widely among famous mountains, then settled on Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 則天聞其名，召至都，降手敕以贊美之。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian heard his reputation, summoned him to the capital, and issued a personal edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu heard of his reputation, summoned him to the capital, and issued a personal edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 及將還，敕麟臺監李嶠餞之於洛橋之東。

translations.literal: When he was about to return, she ordered Director of the Pavilion of Unicorn Records Li Qiao to give him a farewell banquet east of the Luo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to return, she ordered Li Qiao, Director of the Pavilion of Unicorn Records, to give him a farewell banquet east of the Luo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，睿宗令其兄承祎就天臺山追之至京，引入宮中，問以陰陽術數之事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, Ruizong sent his elder brother Chengyi to Mount Tiantai to pursue him and bring him to the capital; he was introduced into the palace and questioned about yin-yang and numerological arts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun, Ruizong sent Chengzhen's elder brother Chengyi to Mount Tiantai to bring him to the capital; he was brought into the palace and questioned about yin-yang and numerological arts.

sentences.zh: 承禎對曰：「道經之旨：『為道日損，損之又損，以至於無為。』

translations.literal: Chengzhen replied: "The gist of the Daoist scripture: 'In pursuing the Way one daily diminishes, diminishing again and again, until one reaches non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen replied, "The gist of the Daoist scripture is: 'In pursuing the Way one daily diminishes, diminishing again and again, until one reaches non-action.

sentences.zh: 且心目所知見者，每損之尚未能已，豈復攻乎異端，而增其智慮哉！」

translations.literal: And what the eyes and mind know and see — to diminish each day I still cannot stop; how much less should one pursue heterodox arts and add to one's cleverness and deliberation!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the eyes and mind know and see — to diminish it each day I still cannot finish; how much less should one pursue heterodox arts and add to one's cleverness and deliberation!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「理身無為，則清高矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Non-action in ordering the person — then one is pure and lofty!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Non-action in ordering the person — then one is pure and lofty!

sentences.zh: 理國無為，如何？」

translations.literal: Non-action in ordering the state — how is that done?"
translations.idiomatic: Non-action in ordering the state — how is that done?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國猶身也。

translations.literal: He replied: "The state is like the person.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The state is like the person.

sentences.zh: 《老子》曰：『遊心於淡，合氣於漠，順物自然而無私焉，而天下理。』

translations.literal: The Laozi says: 'Let the heart roam in simplicity, blend breath with the vast, follow things' nature without selfishness — and all under Heaven is ordered.'
translations.idiomatic: The Laozi says, 'Let the heart roam in simplicity, blend breath with the vast, follow things' nature without selfishness — and all under Heaven is ordered.'

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『聖人者，與天地合其德。』

translations.literal: The Yijing says: 'The sage joins his virtue with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Yijing says, 'The sage joins his virtue with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 是知天不言而信，不為而成。

translations.literal: From this one knows Heaven speaks not yet is trusted, acts not yet completes.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that Heaven speaks not yet is trusted, acts not yet accomplishes.

sentences.zh: 無為之旨，理國之道也。」

translations.literal: The principle of non-action is the Way of ordering the state."
translations.idiomatic: The principle of non-action is the Way of ordering the state."

sentences.zh: 睿宗嘆息曰：「廣成之言，即斯是也！」

translations.literal: Ruizong sighed and said: "The words of Guangcheng — this is exactly it!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong sighed and said, "The words of Guangcheng — this is exactly it!"

sentences.zh: 承禎固辭還山，仍賜寶琴一張，及霞紋帔而遣之，朝中詞人贈詩者百余人。

translations.literal: Chengzhen firmly declined and returned to the mountain. He was still granted one precious zither and a cloud-pattern cape as he was sent off; over a hundred poets at court presented poems.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen firmly declined and returned to the mountains. He was still given a precious zither and a cloud-pattern cape as he was sent off, and more than a hundred poets at court presented poems to him.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，玄宗又遣使迎入京，親受法箓，前後賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong again sent envoys to welcome him to the capital; he personally received the ritual registers; rewards before and after were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong again sent envoys to welcome him to the capital; he personally received the ritual registers, and the rewards before and after were very generous.

sentences.zh: 十年，駕還西都，承禎又請還天臺山，玄宗賦詩以遣之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the imperial carriage returned to the Western Capital, Chengzhen again requested return to Mount Tiantai; Xuanzong composed a poem to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the imperial carriage returned to the Western Capital, Chengzhen again asked to return to Mount Tiantai, and Xuanzong composed a poem to send him off.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又召至都。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was again summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was again summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令承禎於王屋山自選形勝，置壇室以居焉。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Chengzhen to choose for himself a scenic site on Mount Wangwu and establish an altar chamber to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ordered Chengzhen to choose for himself a scenic site on Mount Wangwu and establish an altar chamber to live there.

sentences.zh: 承禎因上言：「今五嶽神祠，皆是山林之神，非正真之神也。

translations.literal: Chengzhen thereupon submitted a memorial: "The shrines of the Five Sacred Peaks today all honor mountain-and-forest spirits, not the true and orthodox spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen thereupon submitted a memorial saying, "The shrines of the Five Sacred Peaks today all honor mountain-and-forest spirits, not the true and orthodox spirits.

sentences.zh: 五嶽皆有洞府，各有上清真人降任其職，山川風雨，陰陽氣序，是所理焉。

translations.literal: Each of the Five Peaks has a cavern palace; in each a Shangqing Perfected One descends to assume office — mountains, rivers, wind, rain, and the yin-yang ordering of qi are what they govern.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the Five Peaks has a cavern palace, and in each a Shangqing Perfected One descends to assume office — mountains, rivers, wind, rain, and the yin-yang ordering of qi are what they govern.

sentences.zh: 冠冕章服，佐從神仙，皆有名數。

translations.literal: Their caps, regalia, and attendant immortals all have fixed names and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Their caps, regalia, and attendant immortals all have fixed names and ranks.

sentences.zh: 請別立齋祠之所。」

translations.literal: I request that separate places for fasting and sacrifice be established."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that separate places for fasting and sacrifice be established."

sentences.zh: 玄宗從其言，因敕五嶽各置真君祠一所，其形象制度，皆令承禎推按道經，創意為之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong followed his advice; he ordered that each of the Five Peaks have one True Lord shrine established, their images and systems all designed by Chengzhen according to Daoist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong followed his advice and ordered one True Lord shrine established at each of the Five Peaks; their images and ritual systems were all designed by Chengzhen according to Daoist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 承禎頗善篆隸書，玄宗令以三體寫《老子經》，因刊正文句，定著五千三百八十言為真本以奏上之。

translations.literal: Chengzhen was quite skilled in seal and clerical script. Xuanzong ordered him to copy the Laozi in the three script styles; he thereby corrected the text and established 5,380 characters as the true version, which he presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen was quite skilled in seal and clerical script. Xuanzong ordered him to copy the Laozi in the three script styles; he corrected the text and established 5,380 characters as the true version, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以承禎王屋所居為陽臺觀，上自題額，遣使送之。

translations.literal: Chengzhen's dwelling on Mount Wangwu was made into Yangtai Abbey; the Emperor personally inscribed the plaque and sent an envoy to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen's dwelling on Mount Wangwu was established as Yangtai Abbey; the Emperor personally inscribed the plaque and sent an envoy to deliver it.

sentences.zh: 賜絹三百匹，以充藥餌之用。

translations.literal: Three hundred bolts of silk were granted to supply his medicinal preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three hundred bolts of silk to supply his medicinal preparations.

sentences.zh: 俄又令玉真公主及光祿卿韋縚至其所居，修金箓齋，復加以錫賫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Princess Yuzhen and the Minister of Imperial Entertainments Wei Tao were ordered to his dwelling to perform a golden-register fasting ritual, and he was again given imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Princess Yuzhen and the Minister of Imperial Entertainments Wei Tao were sent to his dwelling to perform a golden-register fasting ritual, and he received further imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒於王屋山，時年八十九。

translations.literal: That year he died on Mount Wangwu, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died on Mount Wangwu, at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其弟子表稱；

translations.literal: His disciples submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: His disciples submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 「死之日，有雙鶴饒壇，及白雲從壇中湧出，上連於天，而師容色如生。」

translations.literal: "On the day of death, a pair of cranes circled the altar, and white clouds surged from within the altar, joining with Heaven above, while the Master's countenance was as in life."
translations.idiomatic: "On the day of his death, a pair of cranes circled the altar, and white clouds surged from within it, rising to join Heaven above, while the Master's countenance remained as in life."

sentences.zh: 玄宗深嘆之，乃下制曰：「混成不測，入寥自化。

translations.literal: Xuanzong sighed deeply and issued an edict: "The undivided whole cannot be fathomed; entering the vast void, one transforms of oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong sighed deeply and issued an edict: "The undivided whole cannot be fathomed; entering the vast void, one transforms of oneself.

sentences.zh: 雖獨立有象，而至極則冥。

translations.literal: Though standing alone it has form, at the utmost limit it is dark and hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Though standing alone it has form, at the utmost limit it is dark and hidden.

sentences.zh: 故王屋山道士司馬子微，心依道勝，理會玄遠，遍遊名山，密契仙洞。

translations.literal: Thus the Wangwu Mountain Daoist Sima Ziwei, whose heart relied on the triumph of the Way and whose understanding grasped the profound and distant, traveled widely among famous mountains and secretly attuned himself to immortal caverns.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Sima Ziwei, the Daoist of Mount Wangwu, whose heart relied on the triumph of the Way and whose understanding grasped the profound and distant, traveled widely among famous mountains and secretly attuned himself to immortal caverns.

sentences.zh: 存觀其妙，逍遙得意之場；

translations.literal: While living he contemplated its subtlety in the free-roaming realm of fulfilled intent;
translations.idiomatic: While living he contemplated its subtlety in the free-roaming realm of fulfilled intent;

sentences.zh: 亡復其根，宴息無何之境。

translations.literal: in death he returned to his root, resting at ease in the realm of nothing-at-all.
translations.idiomatic: in death he returned to his root, resting at ease in the realm of nothing-at-all.

sentences.zh: 固以名登真格，位在靈官。

translations.literal: Truly his name ascends to the register of perfection, his rank among the spirit officials.
translations.idiomatic: Truly his name ascends to the register of perfection, his rank among the spirit officials.

sentences.zh: 林壑未改，遐霄已曠；

translations.literal: The forests and ravines are unchanged, yet the distant heavens are already empty;
translations.idiomatic: The forests and ravines are unchanged, yet the distant heavens are already empty;

sentences.zh: 言念高烈，有愴於懷。

translations.literal: speaking of his lofty virtue, there is sorrow in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: speaking of his lofty virtue, sorrow fills the heart.

sentences.zh: 宜贈徽章，用光丹箓。

translations.literal: It is fitting to grant him an honorary title, to illuminate his cinnabar register.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to grant him an honorary title, to illuminate his cinnabar register.

sentences.zh: 可銀青光祿大夫，號真一先生。」

translations.literal: He may be made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the style Master Zhenyi."
translations.idiomatic: He is to be made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the style Master Zhenyi."

sentences.zh: 仍為親制碑文。

translations.literal: The Emperor also personally composed an epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also personally composed an epitaph for him.

sentences.zh: 吳筠吳筠，魯中之儒士也。

translations.literal: Wu Yun — Wu Yun was a Confucian scholar of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yun was a Confucian scholar from Lu.

sentences.zh: 少通經，善屬文，舉進士不第。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered the classics and was skilled at literary composition; he took the jinshi examination but did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he mastered the classics and was skilled at literary composition, but he failed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性高潔，不奈流俗。

translations.literal: His nature was lofty and pure; he could not endure the ways of the world.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was lofty and pure, and he could not endure the ways of the world.

sentences.zh: 乃入嵩山，依潘師正為道士，傳正一之法，苦心鉆仰，乃盡通其術。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered Mount Song, followed Pan Shizheng to become a Daoist, received transmission of the Zhengyi methods, and through arduous study mastered all its arts.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon entered Mount Song, became a Daoist under Pan Shizheng, received transmission of the Zhengyi methods, and through arduous study mastered all its arts.

sentences.zh: 開元中，南遊金陵，訪道茅山。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era he traveled south to Jinling and sought the Way on Mount Mao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he traveled south to Jinling and sought the Way on Mount Mao.

sentences.zh: 久之，東遊天臺。

translations.literal: After a long while he traveled east to Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he traveled east to Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 筠尤善著述，在剡與越中文士為詩酒之會，所著歌篇，傳於京師。

translations.literal: Yun was especially skilled at writing; in Shan he joined Yue literary men in gatherings of poetry and wine, and the songs he composed spread to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was especially skilled at writing; in Shan he joined literary men of Yue in gatherings of poetry and wine, and the songs he composed spread to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞其名，遣使征之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong heard his name and sent envoys to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong heard of him and sent envoys to summon him.

sentences.zh: 既至，與語甚悅，令待詔翰林。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Emperor was greatly pleased in conversation with him and appointed him to attend at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the Emperor was greatly pleased in conversation with him and appointed him to attend at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝問以道法，對曰：「道法之精，無如五千言，其諸枝詞蔓說，徒費紙劄耳！」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked him about Daoist methods. He replied: "The essence of Daoist teaching is nowhere better than in the five thousand words; all the branching words and spreading explanations merely waste paper!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked him about Daoist methods. He replied, "The essence of Daoist teaching is nowhere better than in the five thousand words; all the branching words and spreading explanations merely waste paper!"

sentences.zh: 又問神仙修煉之事，對曰：「此野人之事，當以歲月功行求之，非人主之所宜適意。」

translations.literal: He was again asked about the cultivation of immortals. He replied: "This is the business of recluses; it must be sought through years of merit and practice — not a matter in which a ruler should take delight."
translations.idiomatic: He was again asked about the cultivation of immortals. He replied, "This is the business of recluses; it must be sought through years of merit and practice — not a matter in which a ruler should take delight."

sentences.zh: 每與緇黃列坐，朝臣啟奏，筠之所陳，但名教世務而已，間之以諷詠，以達其誠。

translations.literal: Whenever he sat in assembly with monks and Daoists as court ministers presented memorials, what Yun offered was only matters of moral teaching and worldly affairs, interspersed with satirical verse to express his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sat in assembly with monks and Daoists as court ministers presented memorials, what Yun offered concerned only moral teaching and worldly affairs, interspersed with satirical verse to express his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 玄宗深重之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong held him in deep esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong held him in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，李林甫、楊國忠用事，綱紀日紊。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong held power, and government discipline grew daily more disordered.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong held power, and government discipline grew daily more disordered.

sentences.zh: 筠知天下將亂，堅求還嵩山。

translations.literal: Yun knew the realm would soon fall into chaos and firmly requested return to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Yun knew the realm would soon fall into chaos and firmly requested to return to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 累表不許，乃詔於嶽觀別立道院。

translations.literal: Repeated memorials were not granted; an edict then ordered a separate Daoist compound established at the mountain abbey.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated memorials were denied; an edict then ordered a separate Daoist compound established at the mountain abbey.

sentences.zh: 祿山將亂，求還茅山，許之。

translations.literal: As Lushan was about to rebel, he requested return to Mount Mao and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: As Lushan was about to rebel, he requested to return to Mount Mao and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 既而中原大亂，江淮多盜，乃東遊會稽。

translations.literal: Soon the Central Plains fell into great chaos and bandits multiplied along the Yangzi and Huai; he then traveled east to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Central Plains fell into great chaos and bandits multiplied along the Yangzi and Huai; he then traveled east to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 嘗於天臺剡中往來，與詩人李白、孔巢父詩篇酬和，逍遙泉石，人多從之。

translations.literal: He often traveled between Mount Tiantai and Shan, exchanging poems with the poets Li Bai and Kong Chaofu, roaming freely among springs and rocks; many followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He often traveled between Mount Tiantai and Shan, exchanging poems with the poets Li Bai and Kong Chaofu, roaming freely among springs and rocks, and many followed him.

sentences.zh: 竟終於越中。

translations.literal: He ultimately died in Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He ultimately died in Yue.

sentences.zh: 文集二十卷，其《玄綱》三篇、《神仙可學論》等，為達識之士所稱。

translations.literal: His collected works comprise twenty juan; his three essays "Mysterious Principles," "On Whether Immortals Can Be Learned," and the like were praised by men of discerning insight.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works comprise twenty juan; his three essays "Mysterious Principles," "On Whether Immortals Can Be Learned," and the like were praised by men of discerning insight.

sentences.zh: 筠在翰林時，特承恩顧，由是為群僧之所嫉。

translations.literal: When Yun was at the Hanlin Academy he enjoyed special imperial favor, and for this was envied by the Buddhist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was at the Hanlin Academy he enjoyed special imperial favor, and for this was envied by the Buddhist clergy.

sentences.zh: 驃騎高力士素奉佛，嘗短筠於上前，筠不悅，乃求還山。

translations.literal: The Cavalry General Gao Lishi had long been devoted to Buddhism and often spoke ill of Yun before the Emperor; Yun was displeased and requested return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry General Gao Lishi had long been devoted to Buddhism and often spoke ill of Yun before the Emperor; Yun was displeased and requested to return to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 故所著文賦，深詆釋氏，亦為通人所譏。

translations.literal: Therefore the essays and rhapsodies he wrote deeply denounced Buddhism and were also ridiculed by men of broad understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the essays and rhapsodies he wrote deeply denounced Buddhism and were also ridiculed by men of broad understanding.

sentences.zh: 然詞理宏通，文彩煥發，每制一篇，人皆傳寫。

translations.literal: Yet his diction and reasoning were broad and penetrating, his literary brilliance radiant; whenever he composed a piece, everyone copied it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his diction and reasoning were broad and penetrating, his literary brilliance radiant; whenever he composed a piece, everyone copied it.

sentences.zh: 雖李白之放蕩，杜甫之壯麗，能兼之者，其唯筠乎！

translations.literal: Though Li Bai was untrammeled and Du Fu magnificent — who could combine both but Yun!
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Bai was untrammeled and Du Fu magnificent — who else could combine both but Yun!

sentences.zh: 孔述睿孔述睿，趙州人也。

translations.literal: Kong Surui — Kong Surui was a man of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Surui was a man of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖昌宇，膳部郎中。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Changyu was a Director in the Board of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Changyu was a Director in the Board of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 祖舜，監察御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shun was an Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shun was an Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 父齊參，寶鼎令。

translations.literal: His father Qi Can was Magistrate of Baoding County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi Can was Magistrate of Baoding County.

sentences.zh: 述睿少與兄克符、弟克讓，皆事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Surui in youth, with his elder brother Kefu and younger brother Kerang, were all known for serving their parents with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Surui in youth, with his elder brother Kefu and younger brother Kerang, were all known for serving their parents with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 既孤，俱隱於嵩山。

translations.literal: After they were orphaned, all withdrew to seclusion on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: After they were orphaned, all withdrew to seclusion on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 述睿好學不倦，大歷中，轉運使劉晏累表薦述睿有顏、閔之行，遊、夏之學。

translations.literal: Surui loved learning without weariness; during the Dali era the Transport Commissioner Liu Yan repeatedly memorialized recommending Surui for the conduct of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian and the learning of Ziyou and Zixia.
translations.idiomatic: Surui loved learning without weariness; during the Dali era the Transport Commissioner Liu Yan repeatedly memorialized recommending Surui for the conduct of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian and the learning of Ziyou and Zixia.

sentences.zh: 代宗以太常寺協律郎征之。

translations.literal: Daizong summoned him as Harmonizing Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong summoned him as Harmonizing Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 轉國子博士，歷遷尚書司勛員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the National University, then successively promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Erudite of the National University, then successively promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 述睿每加恩命，暫至朝廷謝恩，旬日即辭疾，卻歸舊隱。

translations.literal: Whenever Surui received an additional appointment he would briefly come to court to give thanks; within ten days he would plead illness and return to his former retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Surui received an additional appointment he would briefly come to court to give thanks; within ten days he would plead illness and return to his former retreat.

sentences.zh: 德宗踐祚，以諫議大夫銀章硃綬，命河南尹趙惠伯賫詔書、玄纁束帛，就嵩山以禮征聘。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, he appointed Surui Remonstrance Counselor with silver seal and vermilion cord, and ordered the Henan Prefect Zhao Huibo to carry an edict, dark-and-crimson silk, and ceremonial gifts to Mount Song to summon him with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, he appointed Surui Remonstrance Counselor with silver seal and vermilion cord, and ordered the Henan Prefect Zhao Huibo to carry an edict, dark-and-crimson silk, and ceremonial gifts to Mount Song to summon him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 述睿既至，召對於別殿，特賜第宅，給以廄馬，兼為皇太子侍讀。

translations.literal: When Surui arrived he was summoned for audience in a separate hall, specially granted a residence, given stable horses, and also made Reader to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Surui arrived he was summoned for audience in a separate hall, specially granted a residence, given stable horses, and also made Reader to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 旬日後累表固辭，依前乞還舊山。

translations.literal: After ten days he repeatedly memorialized firmly declining, again requesting return to his old mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days he repeatedly memorialized firmly declining, again requesting to return to his old mountain.

sentences.zh: 詔報之曰：「卿懷伊摯匡時之道，有廣成嘉遁之風。

translations.literal: An edict replied to him: "You bear the Way of Yi Yin and Jie Zhi in aiding the age, and the spirit of Guangcheng in noble withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied to him, "You bear the Way of Yi Yin and Jie Zhi in aiding the age, and the spirit of Guangcheng in noble withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 養素丘園，屢辭命秩。

translations.literal: You cultivate simplicity in garden and grove and have repeatedly declined appointments.
translations.idiomatic: You cultivate simplicity in garden and grove and have repeatedly declined appointments.

sentences.zh: 朕以峒山問道，渭水求師，亦何必務執勞謙，固求退讓！

translations.literal: I, like the Yellow Emperor seeking the Way on Mount Kongtong and like seeking a teacher at the Wei River — why must you insist on laborious humility and firmly seek withdrawal!
translations.idiomatic: I, like the Yellow Emperor seeking the Way on Mount Kongtong and seeking a teacher at the Wei River — why must you insist on laborious humility and firmly seek withdrawal!

sentences.zh: 無違朕旨，且啟乃心。」

translations.literal: Do not go against my intent; open your heart as well."
translations.idiomatic: Do not go against my intent; open your heart as well."

sentences.zh: 述睿既懇辭不獲，方就職。

translations.literal: Surui, having earnestly declined without success, then took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Surui, having earnestly declined without success, then took up his post.

sentences.zh: 久之，改秘書少監，兼右庶子，再加史館修撰。

translations.literal: After a long while he was changed to Vice Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, and again made Compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was changed to Vice Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, and again made Compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 述睿精於地理，在館乃重修《地理志》，時稱詳究。

translations.literal: Surui was expert in geography; while at the Institute he thoroughly revised the "Geographical Treatise," which at the time was called exhaustive and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Surui was expert in geography; while at the Institute he thoroughly revised the "Geographical Treatise," which at the time was called exhaustive and thorough.

sentences.zh: 而又性謙和退讓，與物無競，每親朋集會，嘗恂恂然似不能言者，人皆敬之。

translations.literal: Moreover his nature was modest, gentle, and yielding; he contended with nothing; whenever kin and friends gathered he was always deferential, as though unable to speak — all held him in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his nature was modest, gentle, and yielding; he contended with nothing; whenever kin and friends gathered he was always deferential, as though unable to speak — and all held him in respect.

sentences.zh: 時令狐峘亦充修撰，與述睿同職，多以細碎之事侵述睿，述睿皆讓之，竟不與爭，時人稱為長者。

translations.literal: At the time Linghu Yan also served as compiler, sharing Surui's duties; he often encroached on Surui with petty matters, but Surui always yielded and never contended; men of the time called him an elder of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Linghu Yan also served as compiler, sharing Surui's duties; he often encroached on Surui with petty matters, but Surui always yielded and never contended; men of the time called him an elder of virtue.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，命賫詔並禦饌、衣服數百襲，往平涼盟會處祭陷歿將士骸骨，以述睿性精愨故也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he was ordered to carry an edict together with imperial provisions and several hundred sets of clothing to the site of the Pingliang alliance to sacrifice over the bones of fallen officers and soldiers — because of Surui's scrupulous and sincere nature.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he was ordered to carry an edict together with imperial provisions and several hundred sets of clothing to the site of the Pingliang alliance to sacrifice over the bones of fallen officers and soldiers — because of Surui's scrupulous and sincere nature.

sentences.zh: 九年，以疾上表，請罷官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, citing illness, he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, citing illness, he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 詔不許，報之曰：「朕以卿德重朝端，行敦風俗，不言之教，所賴攸深，未依來請，想宜悉也。」

translations.literal: An edict did not grant it and replied: "I regard your virtue as weighty at court and your conduct as enriching custom; the teaching without words relies deeply upon you — I have not granted your request; I trust you understand."
translations.idiomatic: An edict did not grant it and replied, "I regard your virtue as weighty at court and your conduct as enriching custom; the teaching without words relies deeply upon you — I have not granted your request; I trust you understand."

sentences.zh: 述睿再三上表，方獲允許，乃以太子賓客賜紫金魚袋致仕，放還鄉里。

translations.literal: Surui submitted memorials again and again before permission was granted; he was then made Retired with the title Guest of the Crown Prince, granted a purple-gold fish tally, and released to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Surui submitted memorials again and again before permission was granted; he was then retired with the title Guest of the Crown Prince, granted a purple-gold fish tally, and released to his home district.

sentences.zh: 仍賜帛五十匹，衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was further granted fifty bolts of silk and one set of robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted fifty bolts of silk and one set of robes.

sentences.zh: 故事，致仕還鄉者皆不給公乘，德宗優寵儒者，特命給而遣之。

translations.literal: By precedent, those who retired and returned home were not given official transport; Dezong, showing special favor to Confucian scholars, specially ordered transport provided and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, those who retired and returned home were not given official transport; Dezong, showing special favor to Confucian scholars, specially ordered transport provided and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 貞元十六年九月卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 子敏行。

translations.literal: His son was Minxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Minxing.

sentences.zh: 子 敏行敏行，字至之，舉進士，元和五年禮部侍郎崔樞下擢第。

translations.literal: His son Minxing — Minxing, styled Zhizhi, took the jinshi examination and in the fifth year of Yuanhe passed under Vice Minister of Rites Cui Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Minxing, styled Zhizhi, took the jinshi examination and in the fifth year of Yuanhe passed under Vice Minister of Rites Cui Shu.

sentences.zh: 呂元膺廉問嶽鄂，辟為賓佐。

translations.literal: When Lü Yuanying conducted an inspection of Yue and E, he recruited Minxing as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yuanying conducted an inspection of Yue and E, he recruited Minxing as a staff member.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂而罷。

translations.literal: He resigned upon completing mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned upon completing mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 後元膺為東都留守，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: Later Yuanying became Protector of the Eastern Capital and was transferred to command at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuanying became Protector of the Eastern Capital and was transferred to command at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 敏行皆從之。

translations.literal: Minxing followed him in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: Minxing followed him throughout.

sentences.zh: 十四年，入為右拾遺，遷左補闕。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered court as Right Reminder and was promoted to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he entered court as Right Reminder and was promoted to Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，為起居郎，改左司員外郎，歷司勛郎中，充集賢殿學士，遷吏部郎中，俄拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: During the Changqing era he was Diarist, then changed to Assistant Director in the Left Department, successively served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made Academician of the Jixian Hall, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and soon appointed Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era he was Diarist, then changed to Assistant Director in the Left Department, successively served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made Academician of the Jixian Hall, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and soon appointed Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 上疏論興元監軍楊叔元陰激募卒為亂，殺節度使李絳。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial arguing that the Xingyuan army supervisor Yang Shuyuan had secretly incited recruited soldiers to rebel and had killed the military governor Li Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing that the Xingyuan army supervisor Yang Shuyuan had secretly incited recruited soldiers to rebel and had killed the military governor Li Jiang.

sentences.zh: 人不敢發其事，敏行上表極諍之，故叔元得罪，時論稱美。

translations.literal: No one dared expose the matter; Minxing memorialized with utmost remonstrance, and so Shuyuan was punished — public opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared expose the matter; Minxing memorialized with utmost remonstrance, and so Shuyuan was punished — public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 敏行名臣之子，少而修潔，為人所稱；

translations.literal: Minxing was the son of a famous minister; in youth he was upright and pure and was praised by others;
translations.idiomatic: Minxing was the son of a famous minister; in youth he was upright and pure and was praised by others;

sentences.zh: 及遊宦，與當時豪俊為友。

translations.literal: when he entered official service he befriended the leading men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: when he entered official service he befriended the leading men of the age.

sentences.zh: 雖名華為一時冠，而貞規雅操，與父遠矣。

translations.literal: Though his fame and splendor topped the age, his steadfast principles and elegant conduct fell far short of his father's.
translations.idiomatic: Though his fame and splendor topped the age, his steadfast principles and elegant conduct fell far short of his father's.

sentences.zh: 大和九年正月卒，年四十九，贈尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Dahe he died, aged forty-nine; he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Public Works in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of Dahe he died, at the age of forty-nine; he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Public Works in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陽城陽城，字亢宗，北平人也。

translations.literal: Yang Cheng — Yang Cheng, styled Kangzong, was a man of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng, styled Kangzong, was a man of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 代為宦族。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been an official clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been an official clan.

sentences.zh: 家貧不能得書，乃求為集賢寫書吏，竊官書讀之，晝夜不出房；

translations.literal: His family was poor and could not obtain books; he therefore sought to become a copyist at the Jixian Hall, secretly read the official books, and day and night did not leave his room;
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and could not obtain books; he therefore sought to become a copyist at the Jixian Hall, secretly read the official books, and day and night did not leave his room;

sentences.zh: 經六年，乃無所不通。

translations.literal: after six years there was nothing he had not mastered.
translations.idiomatic: after six years there was nothing he had not mastered.

sentences.zh: 既而隱於中條山。

translations.literal: Thereafter he withdrew to seclusion on Mount Zhongtiao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he withdrew to seclusion on Mount Zhongtiao.

sentences.zh: 遠近慕其德行，多從之學。

translations.literal: Near and far admired his virtue and conduct; many came to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far admired his virtue and conduct; many came to study under him.

sentences.zh: 閭裏相訟者，不詣官府，詣城請決。

translations.literal: When neighbors had lawsuits they did not go to the magistrate but came to Cheng to request judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors had lawsuits they did not go to the magistrate but came to Cheng to request judgment.

sentences.zh: 陜虢觀察使李泌聞其名，親詣其裏訪之，與語甚悅。

translations.literal: The Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner Li Bi heard his name, personally went to his village to visit him, and was greatly pleased in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner Li Bi heard his name, personally went to his village to visit him, and was greatly pleased in conversation.

sentences.zh: 泌為宰相，薦為著作郎。

translations.literal: When Bi became Chancellor he recommended Cheng as Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi became Chancellor he recommended Cheng as Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 德宗令長安縣尉楊寧賫束帛詣夏縣所居而召之，城乃衣褐赴京，上章辭讓。

translations.literal: Dezong ordered the Chang'an County Captain Yang Ning to carry silk gifts to his dwelling in Xia County and summon him; Cheng then wore coarse cloth and went to the capital, submitting a memorial declining.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong ordered the Chang'an County Captain Yang Ning to carry silk gifts to his dwelling in Xia County and summon him; Cheng then wore coarse cloth and went to the capital, submitting a memorial declining.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣中官持章服衣之，而後詔，賜帛五十匹。

translations.literal: Dezong sent a eunuch bearing official robes to clothe him, and only then issued the edict, granting fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sent a eunuch bearing official robes to clothe him, and only then issued the edict, granting fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 初未至京，人皆想望風彩，曰：「陽城山人能自刻苦，不樂名利，今為諫官，必能以死奉職。」

translations.literal: At first, before reaching the capital, everyone looked forward to his wind and color, saying: "Yang Cheng the mountain man can impose hardship upon himself, does not delight in fame and profit; now he is a remonstrating official—he will surely be able to devote himself unto death in fulfilling his office."
translations.idiomatic: Before he even reached the capital, all eyes were on him. People said, "Yang Cheng the recluse of the hills knows how to harden himself against hardship and cares nothing for fame or gain. Now that he holds office as a remonstrance counselor, he will surely serve unto death.

sentences.zh: 人鹹畏憚之。

translations.literal: Everyone both feared and stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: All feared and revered him.

sentences.zh: 及至，諸諫官紛紜言事，細碎無不聞達，天子益厭苦之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the various remonstrating officials spoke on affairs in profusion; trivial details none failed to reach [the throne]; the Son of Heaven grew ever more weary and vexed by it.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the remonstrance officials were already clamoring with petitions on every petty matter until nothing failed to reach the throne, and the emperor grew ever more weary of it.

sentences.zh: 而城方與二弟及客日夜痛飲，人莫能窺其際，皆以虛名譏之。

translations.literal: Yet Cheng was just then drinking heavily day and night with his two younger brothers and guests; no one could fathom his inner mind, and all ridiculed him as a hollow reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Cheng was carousing day and night with his two brothers and their guests. No one could penetrate his purpose, and all mocked him as a man of empty renown.

sentences.zh: 有造城所居，將問其所以者。

translations.literal: There was one who came to Cheng's dwelling, intending to ask his reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Someone came to visit Cheng at his home, intending to ask what he meant by it.

sentences.zh: 城望風知其意，引之與坐，輒強以酒。

translations.literal: Cheng, sensing his purpose at a glance, led him to sit, and repeatedly forced wine upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng saw at once what he wanted and invited him to sit—but only to press wine on him relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 客辭，城輒引自飲；

translations.literal: When the guest declined, Cheng would at once drink it himself;
translations.idiomatic: When the guest refused, Cheng would drink the cup himself;

sentences.zh: 客不能已，乃與城酬酢。

translations.literal: the guest could not stop [declining], and therefore exchanged toasts with Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: until the guest could resist no longer and joined him in toasting back and forth.

sentences.zh: 客或時先醉，臥席上，城或時先醉，臥客懷中，不能聽客語。

translations.literal: Sometimes the guest would first grow drunk and lie upon the mat; sometimes Cheng would first grow drunk and lie in the guest's bosom, unable to listen to the guest's words.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the guest passed out first on the mat; sometimes Cheng passed out first in the guest's arms, too drunk to hear a word the guest said.

sentences.zh: 約其二弟云：「吾所得月俸，汝可度吾家有幾口，月食米當幾何，買薪、菜、鹽凡用幾錢，先具之，其余悉以送酒媼，無留也。」

translations.literal: He told his two younger brothers: "From my monthly salary that I receive, you may calculate how many mouths our household has, how much rice we need each month, and how much money is required altogether for buying firewood, vegetables, and salt—prepare these first; all the rest send entirely to the wine seller's wife, and leave nothing."
translations.idiomatic: He told his two brothers, "Take my monthly salary, figure how many we are at home and how much rice we need, set aside what firewood, vegetables, and salt will cost—and give everything left to the wine seller. Keep nothing back.

sentences.zh: 未嘗有所蓄積。

translations.literal: He never had any savings.
translations.idiomatic: He never saved a penny.

sentences.zh: 雖所服用有切急不可闕者，客稱某物佳可愛，城輒喜，舉而授之。

translations.literal: Even though among what he wore and used there were things urgently needed that could not be done without, if a guest praised some item as fine and lovable, Cheng would at once rejoice, pick it up, and give it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Even things he could hardly do without—if a guest admired something he wore or used, Cheng would delightedly hand it over on the spot.

sentences.zh: 有陳某者，候其始請月俸，常往稱其錢帛之美，月有獲焉。

translations.literal: There was one surnamed Chen who, waiting for the time when [Cheng] first requested his monthly salary, would often go and praise the beauty of his money and silk, and every month had his gain from it.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Chen made a habit of visiting just when Cheng drew his pay, praising the quality of his coins and cloth—and every month walked away with something.

sentences.zh: 時德宗在位，多不假宰相權，而左右得以因緣用事。

translations.literal: At that time Dezong held the throne; he often did not entrust authority to the chancellors, and those at his side were able to use opportunity to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's reign the emperor often withheld power from the chancellors, and his close attendants seized every opening to rule in his name.

sentences.zh: 於是裴延齡、李齊運、韋渠牟尋以奸佞相次進用，誣譖時宰，毀詆大臣，陸贄等鹹遭枉黜，無敢救者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and Wei Qumou soon in succession were promoted for wicked flattery; they slandered the chief ministers of the time, defamed great officials—Lu Zhi and others all suffered wrongful dismissal, and none dared save them.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and Wei Qumou rose one after another through wicked flattery. They framed the chief ministers and vilified the court's great men; Lu Zhi and others were unjustly driven out, and no one dared intervene.

sentences.zh: 城乃伏閣上疏，與拾遺王仲舒共論延齡奸佞，贄等無罪。

translations.literal: Cheng then prostrated himself at the gate and submitted a memorial, together with the Remonstrance Archivist Wang Zhongshu jointly denouncing Yanling's wicked flattery, and [declaring] that Zhi and the others were guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then prostrated himself at the palace gate and submitted a memorial with the Remonstrance Archivist Wang Zhongshu, denouncing Yanling's treachery and declaring Lu Zhi and the others innocent.

sentences.zh: 德宗大怒，召宰相入議，將加城罪。

translations.literal: Dezong was greatly enraged, summoned the chancellors in for deliberation, and was about to impose punishment on Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong flew into a rage, called the chancellors in, and was poised to punish Cheng.

sentences.zh: 時順宗在東宮，為城獨開解之，城賴之獲免。

translations.literal: At that time Shunzong was in the Eastern Palace; he alone spoke in Cheng's defense, and Cheng relied on this to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Shunzong alone spoke in Cheng's defense, and Cheng was spared on his account.

sentences.zh: 於是金吾將軍張萬福聞諫官伏閣諫，趨往，至延英門，大言賀曰：「朝廷有直臣，天下必太平矣！」

translations.literal: Thereupon the Jinwu General Zhang Wanfu, hearing that the remonstrating officials had prostrated at the gate to remonstrate, hurried there; arriving at the Yanying Gate he loudly proclaimed in congratulation: "The court has an upright minister—the realm must surely know great peace!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinwu General Zhang Wanfu heard that the remonstrance officials had taken their protest to the palace gate, he hurried to the Yanying Gate and cried out in celebration: "The court has an upright minister—all under Heaven will soon know peace!

sentences.zh: 乃造城及王仲舒等曰：「諸諫議能如此言事，天下安得不太平？」

translations.literal: Then he went to Cheng and Wang Zhongshu and the others, saying: "If the Remonstrance Counselors can speak on affairs like this, how could the realm not be at great peace?"
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to Cheng and Wang Zhongshu. "If remonstrance counselors speak truth like this," he said, "how can the realm not be at peace?"

sentences.zh: 已而連呼「太平，太平」。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he repeatedly cried "Great peace! Great peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he cried over and over, "Peace! Peace!"

sentences.zh: 萬福武人，年八十余，自此名重天下。

translations.literal: Wanfu was a military man, over eighty years of age; from this his name weighed heavily throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu was a soldier, past eighty—and from that day his name resounded across the empire.

sentences.zh: 時朝夕欲相延齡，城曰：「脫以延齡為相，城當取白麻壞之。」

translations.literal: At that time [the emperor] from morning to evening wished to make Yanling chancellor; Cheng said: "If by chance Yanling should be made chancellor, Cheng will take the white hemp [edict] and destroy it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was daily on the verge of appointing Yanling chancellor. Cheng declared, "If Yanling is made chancellor, I will seize the edict scroll and tear it to pieces.

sentences.zh: 竟坐延齡事改國子司業。

translations.literal: In the end, on account of the Yanling affair, he was transferred to be Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was demoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education over the Yanling affair.

sentences.zh: 城既至國學，乃召諸生，告之曰：「凡學者所以學，為忠與孝也。

translations.literal: Once Cheng had arrived at the Imperial Academy, he summoned the students and told them: "Whatever students study, they study for the sake of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng took up his post at the Imperial Academy, he summoned the students and told them: "You study for one reason—to learn loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 諸生寧有久不省其親者乎？」

translations.literal: Among you students, could there be any who for long have not visited their parents?"
translations.idiomatic: Is there among you anyone who has long neglected his parents?

sentences.zh: 明日，告城歸養者二十余人。

translations.literal: The next day, more than twenty reported to Cheng that they wished to return home to care for their parents.
translations.idiomatic: The next day more than twenty asked leave to go home and nurse their parents.

sentences.zh: 有薛約者，嘗學於城，性狂躁，以言事得罪，徙連州，客寄無根蒂。

translations.literal: There was one named Xue Yue who had once studied under Cheng; by nature wild and restless, he offended through speaking on affairs, was exiled to Lian Prefecture, and as a sojourner had no root or foothold.
translations.idiomatic: A former student named Xue Yue—restless and hot-tempered—had offended the throne by speaking out and been banished to Lianzhou, a stranger far from home with nowhere to land.

sentences.zh: 臺吏以蹤跡求得之於城家。

translations.literal: The censorial officers followed his tracks and found him at Cheng's house.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officers tracked him down to Cheng's home.

sentences.zh: 城坐臺吏於門，與約飲酒訣別，涕泣送之郊外。

translations.literal: Cheng seated the censorial officers at the gate, drank a farewell cup with Yue, and with tears escorted him to the outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had the officers wait at the gate while he shared a farewell cup with Yue, then walked him out of the city weeping.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞之，以城黨罪人，出為道州刺史。

translations.literal: Dezong heard of this and, holding that Cheng had fraternized with a criminal, sent him out as prefect of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong learned of it, he judged Cheng guilty of sheltering a criminal and banished him to be prefect of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 太學生王魯卿、季償等二百七十人詣闕乞留，經數日，吏遮止之，疏不得上。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy students Wang Luqing, Ji Chang, and more than two hundred seventy others went to the palace gate begging that Cheng be retained; after several days officials blocked and stopped them, and their memorial could not be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred seventy Imperial Academy students, led by Wang Luqing and Ji Chang, petitioned at the palace gate to keep Cheng at court; for days officials barred their way and the memorial never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 在道州，以家人法待吏人，宜罰者罰之，宜賞者賞之，不以簿書介意。

translations.literal: In Daozhou, he treated officials and the people by the methods of a household head: those who deserved punishment he punished, those who deserved reward he rewarded, and he did not mind about ledgers and documents.
translations.idiomatic: At Daozhou he governed officials and commoners as a head of household would: punishing when punishment was due, rewarding when reward was due, with little thought for paperwork.

sentences.zh: 道州土地產民多矮，每年常配鄉戶，竟以其男號為「矮奴」。

translations.literal: Daozhou's land produced people mostly of short stature; each year village households were regularly assigned [for tribute], and in the end their males were called "dwarf slaves."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Daozhou tended to be short of stature; every year rural households were levied to supply tribute, and their sons were listed as "dwarf slaves."

sentences.zh: 城下車，禁以良為賤，又憫其編甿歲有離異之苦，乃抗疏論而免之，自是乃停其貢。

translations.literal: When Cheng descended from his carriage [took office], he forbade treating the good as base; he also pitied the registered common folk who each year suffered the pain of separation, and therefore submitted a bold memorial arguing [against it] and secured exemption—from this the tribute was halted.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Cheng forbade treating free men as chattel and, grieving the annual wrench of families torn apart, submitted a bold memorial that ended the levy—and the tribute ceased.

sentences.zh: 民皆賴之，無不泣荷。

translations.literal: The people all relied on him; none failed to weep in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: The people blessed him; all wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 前刺史有贓罪。

translations.literal: The previous prefect had a crime of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: The former prefect was guilty of embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 觀察使方推鞫之，吏有幸於前刺史者，拾其不法事以告，自為功，城立杖殺之。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner was just then pressing the investigation; an official who had been favored by the previous prefect gathered his unlawful deeds to report, seeking credit for himself—Cheng immediately had him beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: While the observation commissioner was investigating, a clerk who had curried favor with the former prefect gathered evidence of his crimes to claim credit—Cheng had him beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 賦稅不登，觀察使數加誚讓。

translations.literal: Taxes were not collected in full; the observation commissioner repeatedly added reproach and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Tax returns fell short, and the observation commissioner rebuked him again and again.

sentences.zh: 州上考功第，城自署其第曰：「撫字心勞，征科政拙，考下下。」

translations.literal: The prefecture submitted its merit evaluation grade; Cheng himself inscribed his grade, saying: "In governing and nurturing the people my heart labored; in collecting taxes my administration was clumsy—evaluation: lowest of the low."
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture filed its merit rating, Cheng wrote his own grade: "Governing the people with a weary heart, collecting taxes with a clumsy hand—lowest of the low.

sentences.zh: 觀察使遣判官督其賦，至州，怪城不出迎，以問州吏。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner dispatched a reviewing official to supervise his tax collection; when he reached the prefecture, he wondered that Cheng did not come out to welcome him, and asked the prefectural clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner sent a staff reviewer to press for taxes. When he arrived, Cheng did not come out to greet him, and the reviewer asked the clerks why.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「刺史聞判官來，以為有罪，自囚於獄，不敢出。」

translations.literal: The clerks said: "When the prefect heard the reviewing official was coming, he thought himself guilty and imprisoned himself in jail, not daring to come out."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "When our prefect heard you were coming, he took himself for a criminal and locked himself in the jail.

sentences.zh: 判官大驚，馳入謁城於獄，曰：「使君何罪！

translations.literal: The reviewing official was greatly alarmed, galloped in to visit Cheng in the jail, and said: "Prefect, what crime [have you committed]!
translations.idiomatic: The reviewer was aghast. He rushed into the jail and found Cheng. "What crime have you committed, my lord?

sentences.zh: 某奉命來候安否耳。」

translations.literal: I have received orders merely to inquire after your well-being."
translations.idiomatic: I am here only to inquire after your health."

sentences.zh: 留一二日未去，城因不復歸館；

translations.literal: He stayed one or two days without leaving; Cheng therefore did not return to the guest quarters;
translations.idiomatic: When the reviewer lingered a day or two, Cheng refused to return to the official guesthouse;

sentences.zh: 門外有故門扇橫地，城晝夜坐臥其上，判官不自安，辭去。

translations.literal: outside the gate an old door panel lay across the ground; Cheng day and night sat and slept upon it—the reviewing official felt ill at ease and took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: instead he day and night sat and slept on an old door panel lying in the yard until the unnerved reviewer departed.

sentences.zh: 其後又遣他判官往按之，他判官義不欲按，乃載妻子行，中道而自逸。

translations.literal: Afterward [the commissioner] again sent another reviewing official to investigate him; the other reviewing official, on principle unwilling to investigate, loaded his wife and children and set out, but midway on the road absconded of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Another reviewer was dispatched; unwilling on principle to carry out the investigation, he set out with his family—and vanished halfway there.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，詔征之，而城已卒。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, an edict summoned him—but Cheng had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne he issued a summons to recall Cheng—but Cheng was already dead.

sentences.zh: 士君子惜之，是歲四月，賜其家錢二百貫文，仍令所在州縣給遞，以喪歸葬焉。

translations.literal: Men of honor grieved for him; in the fourth month of that year [the court] granted his household two hundred strings of cash, and further ordered the prefectures and counties along the way to provide relay transport, that his coffin might return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars mourned him. That April the court granted his family two hundred strings of cash and ordered every prefecture and county along the route to furnish relay couriers so his remains might be carried home for burial.

sentences.zh: 崔覲崔覲，梁州城固人。

translations.literal: Cui Xian—Cui Xian was a man of Chenggu in Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian was a native of Chenggu in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為儒不樂仕進，以耕稼為業。

translations.literal: As a Confucian he took no joy in advancing in office and made farming his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucian scholar, he shunned official advancement and lived by the plow.

sentences.zh: 老而無子，乃以田宅家財分給奴婢，令各為生業。

translations.literal: Growing old without sons, he then divided fields, houses, and household wealth among his slaves and maidservants, ordering each to make a living trade.
translations.idiomatic: Childless in old age, he divided his fields, house, and fortune among his servants and freed them to make their own livings.

sentences.zh: 覲夫妻遂隱於城固南山，家事不問。

translations.literal: Xian and his wife then withdrew to seclusion on the southern mountains of Chenggu and did not inquire into household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He and his wife retired to the southern hills of Chenggu and left all household matters behind.

sentences.zh: 約奴婢遞過其舍，至則供給酒食而已。

translations.literal: He arranged that slaves and maidservants should in turn pass by his dwelling; when they arrived he merely supplied wine and food, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Former servants were to visit in rotation; when they came he offered wine and a meal—and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 夫婦林泉相對，以嘯詠自娛。

translations.literal: Husband and wife faced each other amid forest and spring, taking whistling and chanting for their amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Man and wife faced each other among woods and streams, amusing themselves with song and verse.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使鄭余慶高其行，辟為節度參謀，累邀方至府第。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing, military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, esteemed his conduct and summoned him as military staff officer; only after repeated invitations did he finally reach the commissioner's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing, commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, admired his character and invited him as a staff officer—but only after many summonses did Xian come to the commissioner's gate.

sentences.zh: 為吏無方略，苦不達人事，余慶以長者優容之。

translations.literal: Serving as an official he had no strategy or method; he suffered from not understanding human affairs—Yuqing as an elder treated him with generous forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He proved hopeless at administration and painfully inept with people; Yuqing indulged him as one indulges an elder.

sentences.zh: 太和八年，左補闕王直方上疏論事，得召見，文宗便殿訪以時事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe, the Left Remonstrance Supplementation Censor Wang Zhifang submitted a memorial discussing affairs, was granted an audience, and in the Wenzong emperor's informal hall was consulted on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taihe the Left Supplementation Remonstrance Censor Wang Zhifang memorialized on state affairs, was summoned to audience, and in Emperor Wenzong's private hall was questioned on the times.

sentences.zh: 直方亦興元人，與覲城固山為鄰，是日因薦覲有高行，詔以起居郎征之。

translations.literal: Zhifang was also a man of Xingyuan, neighbor to Xian on Chenggu Mountain; that day he therefore recommended Xian as a man of lofty conduct, and an edict summoned him as Diary Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang was also from Xingyuan and lived near Xian in the Chenggu hills; that day he recommended Xian for his exalted character, and the throne summoned him as Diary Archivist.

sentences.zh: 覲辭疾不起。

translations.literal: Xian declined on grounds of illness and did not rise [to office].
translations.idiomatic: Xian pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 卒於山。

translations.literal: He died in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the hills.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高士忘懷，不隱不顯。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Lofty men forget their cares—neither hiding nor displaying themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The lofty soul forgets itself—neither hidden nor on display.

sentences.zh: 依隱釣名，真風漸鮮。

translations.literal: Leaning on seclusion to angle for fame—the true wind gradually grows rare.
translations.idiomatic: Those who feign retirement to fish for renown have thinned the age's true integrity.

sentences.zh: 結廬泉石，投紱市朝。

translations.literal: Building huts amid springs and rocks, casting off the seal at court and market.
translations.idiomatic: Some build huts among springs and stone; others cast off their seals in the halls of power.

sentences.zh: 心無出處，是曰逍遙。

translations.literal: When the heart has no dwelling in "going forth" or "withdrawing"—this is called free roaming.
translations.idiomatic: When the heart no longer cares whether to serve or withdraw—that is true freedom.
